verses.1:1: And it happened after Saul died that David returned, striking Amalek; and David stayed in Ziklag two days.
verses.1:2: And it happened on the third day that, look, a man came from the camp, from the people of Saul, and his garments were torn and earth was on his head; and it happened when he came in to David that he fell to the ground and bowed down to him.
verses.1:3: And David said to him, "Where are you coming from?" And he said to him, "From the camp of Israel I have escaped."
verses.1:4: And David said to him, "What is this matter? Report to me." And he said, "The people fled from the battle, and many from the people have fallen and died; and Saul also died, and Jonathan his son died."
verses.1:5: And David said to the young man who was reporting to him, "How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?"
verses.1:6: And the young man who was reporting to him said, "By chance they happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and look, Saul was leaning on his spear, and look, the chariots and the cavalry commanders closed in on him.
verses.1:7: And he looked behind him, and saw and called me, and I said, 'Here I am.'
verses.1:8: And he said to me, 'Who are you?' And I said, 'I am an Amalekite.'
verses.1:9: And he said to me, 'Stand over me now and put me to death, for a terrible darkness has seized me, because all my life is in me.'
verses.1:10: And I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he would not live after he fell; and I took the royal crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."
verses.1:11: And David took hold of his garments and tore them, and all the men who were with him tore their garments.
verses.1:12: And they mourned and fasted and wept until evening over Saul and over Jonathan his son, and over the people of Judah, and over the house of Israel, because they were struck down by the sword.
verses.1:13: And David said to the young man who was reporting to him, "Where are you from?" And he said, "I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite man."
verses.1:14: And David said to him, "How were you not afraid to raise your hand to destroy the anointed of the Lord?"
verses.1:15: And David called one of his young men and said, "Approach and fall upon him." And he struck him, and he died.
verses.1:16: And David said to him, "Your blood be on your head, because your mouth answered against you, saying, 'I put to death the anointed of the Lord.'"
verses.1:17: And David lamented this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son,
verses.1:18: and he said to teach the sons of Judah; look, it is written in the Book of the Upright:
verses.1:19: "Set up a monument, Israel, for those who have died, wounded on your heights! How mighty men have fallen!
verses.1:20: Do not announce it in Gath, and do not proclaim good news in the thoroughfares of Ashkelon, so that daughters of foreigners may not rejoice, so that daughters of the uncircumcised may not exult.
verses.1:21: Mountains that are in Gilboa, let no dew come down and no rain upon you, nor fields of firstfruits; for there the shield of mighty men was abhorred; the shield of Saul was not anointed with oil.
verses.1:22: From the blood of the wounded, from the fat of mighty men, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back empty, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
verses.1:23: Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and lovely ones, not separated, graceful in their life, and in their death they were not separated; swifter than eagles, and they were stronger than lions.
verses.1:24: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul; weep for the one who clothed you in scarlet with your adornment, the one who placed golden adornment upon your clothing.
verses.1:25: How mighty men have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan, wounded ones are on your heights!
verses.1:26: I grieve over you, my brother Jonathan; you were very lovely to me. Your love to me was made marvelous, beyond the love of women.
verses.1:27: How mighty men have fallen, and weapons of war have perished!"
verses.2:1: And it happened after these things that David inquired of the Lord, saying, "Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?" And the Lord said to him, "Go up." And David said, "Where shall I go up?" And He said, "To Hebron."
verses.2:2: And David went up there to Hebron, and both of his wives, Ahinoam the Israelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite,
verses.2:3: and the men who were with him, each one and his household; and they lived in the cities of Hebron.
verses.2:4: And men of Judea came and anointed David there to reign over the house of Judah. And they reported to David, saying that the men of Jabesh of Gilead had buried Saul.
verses.2:5: And David sent messengers to the leaders of Jabesh of Gilead, and said to them, "Blessed are you by the Lord, because you have shown the mercy of God toward your lord Saul, and buried him.
verses.2:6: And now may the Lord show mercy and truth with you, and I also will do this good thing with you, because you did this thing.
verses.2:7: And now let your hands be strengthened, and become mighty sons, for your lord Saul is dead, and moreover the house of Judah has anointed me as king over itself."
verses.2:8: And Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Saul, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him up from the camp to Mahanaim,
verses.2:9: and made him king over Gilead, and over Thaseiri, and over Israel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.2:10: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years, except for the house of Judah, who followed David.
verses.2:11: And the days that David reigned in Hebron over the house of Judah were seven years and six months.
verses.2:12: And Abner son of Ner and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon;
verses.2:13: and Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out from Hebron and met them at the spring of Gibeon together; and these sat down by the spring of Gibeon on one side, and those by the spring on the other side.
verses.2:14: And Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men arise now and play before us." And Joab said, "Let them arise."
verses.2:15: And they arose and came forward by number: twelve of the servants of Benjamin belonging to Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.
verses.2:16: And each one seized with his hand the head of his fellow, with his sword into the side of his fellow, and they fell together; and the name of that place was called Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gibeon.
verses.2:17: And the battle became exceedingly fierce on that day; and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before the servants of David.
verses.2:18: And three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab and Abishai and Asahel; and Asahel was swift on his feet like one gazelle in a field.
verses.2:19: And Asahel pursued after Abner, and he did not turn aside to go to the right or to the left from behind Abner.
verses.2:20: And Abner looked behind him and said, "Is that you yourself, Asahel?" And he said, "I am."
verses.2:21: And Abner said to him, "Turn aside to the right or to the left, and seize for yourself one of the young men, and take for yourself his full armor." And Asahel was not willing to turn aside from behind him.
verses.2:22: And Abner again spoke to Asahel, saying, "Turn away from me, so that I do not strike you to the ground; and how shall I lift up my face to Joab?
verses.2:23: And where are these things? Turn back to Joab your brother." And he was not willing to turn away. And Abner struck him with the back end of the spear in the loin, and the spear came out through his back, and he fell there and died underneath him; and it happened that everyone who came to the place where Asahel fell and died stood still.
verses.2:24: And Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner, and the sun was setting; and they came as far as the hill of Amman, which is facing Gai, by the wilderness road of Gibeon.
verses.2:25: And the sons of Benjamin who were behind Abner gathered together, and they became one gathering and stood on the top of one hill.
verses.2:26: And Abner called to Joab and said, "Will the sword devour to victory? Or do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? And how long will you not tell the people to turn back from behind our brothers?"
verses.2:27: And Joab said, "As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, then surely from morning the people would have gone up, each one from behind his brother."
verses.2:28: And Joab blew the trumpet, and all the people turned away and did not pursue after Israel, and they did not continue any longer to fight.
verses.2:29: And Abner and his men went off toward the west all that night, and crossed the Jordan and marched through the entire stretch, and came to the camp.
verses.2:30: And Joab turned back from behind Abner and gathered all the people together, and nineteen men of the servants of David were missing.
verses.2:31: And Asahel and the servants of David struck down from the sons of Benjamin, from the men of Abner, three hundred and sixty men from him.
verses.2:32: And they took up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father in Bethlehem; and Joab and the men who were with him marched all night, and day dawned for them in Hebron.
verses.3:1: And the war continued for a long time between the house of Saul and the house of David; and the house of David kept going on and growing stronger, and the house of Saul kept going on and growing weaker.
verses.3:2: And sons were born to David in Hebron; and his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Israelite,
verses.3:3: and his second, Daluia, by Abigail the Carmelite, and the third, Absalom son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur,
verses.3:4: and the fourth, Orneil son of Pheggith, and the fifth, Shephatiah, by Abital,
verses.3:5: and the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.3:6: And it happened, while the war was going on between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner was holding power over the house of Saul.
verses.3:7: And Saul had a concubine, Rizpah daughter of Ial; and Mephibosheth son of Saul said to Abner, "Why did you go in to my father's concubine?"
verses.3:8: And Abner became very angry about Mephibosheth's word, and Abner said to him, "Am I a dog's head? I have shown mercy today to the house of Saul your father, and toward brothers and acquaintances, and I have not defected to the house of David; and do you call me to account concerning a woman's wrongdoing today?
verses.3:9: May God do so to Abner and add still more to him, for just as the Lord swore to David, surely so I will do for him on this day:
verses.3:10: to remove the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."
verses.3:11: And Mephibosheth could no longer answer Abner a word, because he feared him.
verses.3:12: And Abner sent messengers to David at Thailam, where he was, immediately, saying, "Make your covenant with me, and look, my hand is with you to turn the whole house of Israel to you."
verses.3:13: And David said, "Very well, I will make a covenant with you; only one thing I ask from you, saying, 'You will not see my face unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.'"
verses.3:14: And David sent messengers to Mephibosheth son of Saul, saying, "Give back to me my wife Michal, whom I took for one hundred foreskins of foreigners."
verses.3:15: And Mephibosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Paltiel son of Selles.
verses.3:16: And her husband went with her, weeping behind her as far as Baraki; and Abner said to him, "Go, turn back." And he turned back.
verses.3:17: And Abner spoke to the elders of Israel, saying, "Yesterday and the day before you were seeking David to reign over you.
verses.3:18: And now do it, for the Lord spoke concerning David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will save Israel from the hand of foreigners and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
verses.3:19: And Abner spoke in the ears of Benjamin; and Abner went to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that was pleasing in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of the whole house of Benjamin.
verses.3:20: And Abner came to David in Hebron, and with him twenty men; and David made a banquet for Abner and for the men who were with him.
verses.3:21: And Abner said to David, "I will now arise and go, and I will gather all Israel to my lord the king, and I will make a covenant with him, and you will reign over all that your soul desires." And David sent Abner away, and they went in peace.
verses.3:22: And look, the servants of David and Joab were arriving from the raid, and they brought much plunder with them; and Abner was not with David in Hebron, because he had sent him away and he had departed in peace.
verses.3:23: And Joab and all his army arrived, and it was reported to Joab, saying, "Abner son of Ner has come to David, and he has sent him away, and he went away in peace."
verses.3:24: And Joab went in to the king and said, "What is this you have done? Look, Abner came to you, and why have you sent him away, and he has departed in peace?
verses.3:25: Or do you not know the wickedness of Abner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to know everything that you do?"
verses.3:26: And Joab turned back from David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah; and David did not know.
verses.3:27: And he brought Abner back to Hebron, and Joab turned him aside to the side of the gate to speak to him, lying in ambush; and he struck him there in the loin, and he died for the blood of Asahel, Joab's brother.
verses.3:28: And David heard after these things and said, "I and my kingdom are innocent before the Lord and forever of the bloodshed of Abner son of Ner.
verses.3:29: May it come down upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house, and may there never cease from the house of Joab one who has a discharge, or a leper, or one who grasps a staff, or one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread."
verses.3:30: Now Joab and Abishai his brother were keeping close watch on Abner, because he had put to death Asahel their brother in Gibeon in the war.
verses.3:31: And David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your garments and wrap yourselves in sackcloth and mourn before Abner." And King David walked behind the bier.
verses.3:32: And they buried Abner in Hebron; and the king lifted up his voice and wept at his tomb, and all the people wept over Abner.
verses.3:33: And the king lamented over Abner and said, "Should Abner die like the death of Nabal?
verses.3:34: Your hands were not bound, your feet were not in fetters; he did not draw near like Nabal, before sons of injustice you fell." And all the people gathered together to weep for him.
verses.3:35: And all the people came to serve David a funeral meal of bread while it was still day; and David swore, saying, "May God do so to me and add still more, for unless the sun goes down, I will by no means taste bread or anything at all."
verses.3:36: And all the people took note, and everything that the king did before the people was pleasing before them.
verses.3:37: And all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it did not come from the king to put Abner son of Ner to death.
verses.3:38: And the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a great leader has fallen on this day in Israel?
verses.3:39: And that I am today a relative and appointed by a king? But these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too harsh for me; may the Lord repay the one who does evil according to his wickedness."
verses.4:1: And Mephibosheth son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, and his hands grew weak, and all the men of Israel grew faint.
verses.4:2: And Mephibosheth son of Saul had two men who were leaders of raiding bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the second was Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from the sons of Benjamin, for Beeroth was reckoned to the sons of Benjamin.
verses.4:3: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and they were living there as resident aliens until this day.
verses.4:4: Now Jonathan son of Saul had a son who was stricken in his feet; he was five years old when the report of Saul and Jonathan his son came from Israel, and his nurse picked him up and fled; and it happened, as he hurried and withdrew, that he fell and became lame; and his name was Mephibosheth.
verses.4:5: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and entered the house of Mephibosheth in the heat of the day, and he was sleeping in bed at midday.
verses.4:6: And look, the female doorkeeper of the house was cleaning wheat, and she grew drowsy and slept; and Rechab and Baanah the brothers slipped past unnoticed,
verses.4:7: and they went into the house, and Mephibosheth was sleeping on his bed in his bedroom; and they struck him and put him to death, and removed his head, and took his head and went away by the road toward the west all night.
verses.4:8: And they brought the head of Mephibosheth to David in Hebron, and said to the king, "Here is the head of Mephibosheth son of Saul your enemy, who was seeking your life; and the Lord has given to the lord king vengeance on his enemies as on this day, from Saul your enemy and from his seed."
verses.4:9: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from all distress, the one who reported to me that Saul was dead,
verses.4:10: and he was like one bringing good news before me, yet I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, the one to whom I was supposed to give a reward for good news.
verses.4:11: And now wicked men have killed a righteous man in his house upon his bed; and now I will require his blood from your hand and wipe you out from the earth."
verses.4:12: And David commanded his young men, and they killed them; and they cut off their hands and their feet and hung them by the spring in Hebron, and they buried the head of Mephibosheth in the tomb of Abner son of Ner.
verses.5:1: And all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said to him, "Look, we are your bones and your flesh.
verses.5:2: Both yesterday and the day before, while Saul was king over us, you were the one leading out and bringing in Israel; and the Lord said to you, 'You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be leader over Israel.'"
verses.5:3: And all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord, and they anointed David as king over all Israel.
verses.5:4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for forty years.
verses.5:5: For seven years and six months he reigned in Hebron over Judah, and for thirty-three years he reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.
verses.5:6: And David and his men departed for Jerusalem, to the Jebusite who inhabited the land; and it was said to David, "You will not enter here," because the blind and the lame stood in opposition, saying, "David will not enter here."
verses.5:7: And David captured the stronghold of Zion; this is the city of David.
verses.5:8: And David said on that day, "Everyone who strikes a Jebusite, let him attack with a dagger both the lame and the blind and those who hate the soul of David." Therefore they will say, "The blind and the lame will not enter the house of the Lord."
verses.5:9: And David settled in the stronghold, and it was called the city of David; and he built it as a city all around from the citadel, and his own house.
verses.5:10: And David went on advancing and growing great, and the Lord Almighty was with him.
verses.5:11: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar timbers, and craftsmen of wood and craftsmen of stone, and they built a house for David.
verses.5:12: And David knew that the Lord had prepared him as king over Israel, and that his kingdom had been exalted for the sake of His people Israel.
verses.5:13: And David took more wives and concubines from Jerusalem after he came to Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.
verses.5:14: And these are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
verses.5:15: and Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, and Japhia,
verses.5:16: and Elishama, Epidae, and Eliphaath; Samae, Jessibath, Nathan, Galamaan, Jebaar, Theesus, Elphalat, Naged, Nepheg, Janatha, Leasamys, Baalimath, Eliphaath.
verses.5:17: And the foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David; and David heard and went down to the stronghold.
verses.5:18: And the foreigners came and converged on the Valley of the Titans.
verses.5:19: And David inquired through the Lord, saying, "Should I go up against the foreigners, and will You deliver them into my hands?" And the Lord said to David, "Go up, for I will certainly deliver the foreigners into your hands."
verses.5:20: And David came from the Upper Breaches and struck the foreigners there, and David said, "The Lord has broken through the hostile foreigners before me as waters break through." Therefore the name of that place was called Upper Breaches.
verses.5:21: And they left their gods there, and David and the men who were with him took them.
verses.5:22: And the foreigners went up yet again and converged in the Valley of the Titans.
verses.5:23: And David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, "You must not go up to meet them; turn away from them, and you will come upon them near the place of weeping.
verses.5:24: And it will be, when you hear the sound of the closing in from the grove of weeping, then you will go down against them, for then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle of the foreigners."
verses.5:25: And David did just as the Lord commanded him, and he struck down the foreigners from Gibeon as far as the land of Gezer.
verses.6:1: And David again gathered every young man from Israel, about seventy thousand.
verses.6:2: And David arose and went, and all the people who were with him, from the rulers of Judah in an ascent, to bring up from there the ark of God, over which was called the name of the Lord of powers, who sits upon the cherubim on it.
verses.6:3: And he placed the ark of the Lord on a new cart and carried it to the house of Amminadab, who was on the hill; and Uzzah and his brothers, the sons of Amminadab, drove the cart with the ark,
verses.6:4: and his brothers were walking before the ark.
verses.6:5: And David and the sons of Israel were celebrating before the Lord with tuned instruments, with strength, and with songs, and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with flutes.
verses.6:6: And they came as far as the threshing floor of Nodab; and Uzzah stretched out his hand to the ark of God to hold it, and he grasped it, because the calf pulled him aside, in order to hold it.
verses.6:7: And the Lord became angry with Uzzah, and God struck him there, and he died there beside the ark of the Lord before God.
verses.6:8: And David became disheartened because the Lord had broken through with a breach against Uzzah; and that place was called Breach of Uzzah until this day.
verses.6:9: And David feared the Lord on that day, saying, "How will the ark of the Lord come in to me?"
verses.6:10: And David was not willing to turn the ark of the covenant of the Lord aside to himself into the city of David; and David turned it aside into the house of Abeddara the Gittite.
verses.6:11: And the ark of the Lord remained in the house of Abeddara the Gittite for three months; and the Lord blessed the whole house of Abeddara and all that belonged to him.
verses.6:12: And it was reported to King David, saying, "The Lord has blessed the house of Abeddara and all that belongs to him on account of the ark of God." And David went and brought up the ark of the Lord from the house of Abeddara to the city of David with gladness.
verses.6:13: And with them, carrying the ark, were seven choirs, and as a sacrifice, a calf and a lamb.
verses.6:14: And David was playing music with tuned instruments before the Lord, and David was wearing an unusual robe.
verses.6:15: And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and with the sound of a trumpet.
verses.6:16: And it happened, as the ark was coming as far as the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul was looking out through the window, and she saw King David dancing and playing music before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart.
verses.6:17: And they brought the ark of the Lord and set it in its place in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and he offered for it whole burnt offerings before the Lord, and peace offerings.
verses.6:18: And David finished offering up the whole burnt offerings and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of powers.
verses.6:19: And he distributed to all the people, to all the host of Israel from Dan to Beersheba, from man to woman, to each a loaf of bread, and a hearth-baked cake, and a flat cake from a frying pan; and all the people departed, each to his own house.
verses.6:20: And David returned to bless his own house, and Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and blessed him and said, "How the king of Israel has been honored today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the maidservants of his own servants, just as one of the dancers completely uncovers himself!"
verses.6:21: And David said to Michal, "Before the Lord I will dance! Blessed be the Lord, who chose me above your father and above all his house, to appoint me as leader over His people, over Israel. And I will celebrate and dance before the Lord,
verses.6:22: and I will uncover myself still like this, and I will be worthless in your eyes, and with the maidservants about whom you said that I was honored."
verses.6:23: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child until the day she died.
verses.7:1: And it happened when the king settled in his house, and the Lord gave him an inheritance all around from all his enemies who were all around,
verses.7:2: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look now, I live in a cedar house, and the ark of God sits in the middle of the tent."
verses.7:3: And Nathan said to the king, "Everything that is in your heart, go and do, for the Lord is with you."
verses.7:4: And it happened during that night that a word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
verses.7:5: "Go and say to My servant David, 'Thus says the Lord: You will not build a house for Me to live in.
verses.7:6: For I have not lived in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up out of Egypt until this day, and I was walking about in a lodging and in a tent.
verses.7:7: In all the places through which I passed among all Israel, did I speak at all to a single tribe of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built Me a cedar house?"'
verses.7:8: And now thus you will say to My servant David: 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold for you to be a leader over My people, over Israel,
verses.7:9: and I was with you wherever you went, and I utterly destroyed all your enemies from before you, and I made you renowned, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.7:10: And I will appoint a place for My people Israel and plant them, and they will dwell on their own and will no longer be anxious, and a son of unrighteousness will no longer continue to humble them as from the beginning,
verses.7:11: from the days when I appointed judges over My people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will declare to you that you will build a house for Him.
verses.7:12: And it will be, when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, who will come from your own body, and I will prepare his kingdom.
verses.7:13: He will build Me a house for My name, and I will establish his throne forever.
verses.7:14: I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. And if his unrighteousness comes, then I will reprove him with a rod of men and with blows of the sons of men,
verses.7:15: yet I will not remove My mercy from him, as I removed it from those whom I removed from before Me.
verses.7:16: And his house and his kingdom will be confirmed forever before Me, and his throne will be established forever.'"
verses.7:17: According to all these words and according to this entire vision, thus Nathan spoke to David.
verses.7:18: Then King David went in and sat before the Lord, and said, "Who am I, my Lord, Lord, and what is my house, that You have loved me up to these things?
verses.7:19: And I was diminished a little before You, my Lord, yet You spoke concerning the house of Your servant for the distant future; and this is the law of man, my Lord, Lord.
verses.7:20: And what more will David add to speak to You? And now You know Your servant, Lord.
verses.7:21: Because of Your servant You have acted; and according to Your heart You did all this greatness, to make it known to Your servant, for the sake of magnifying You,
verses.7:22: Lord, my Lord. For there is no one like You, and there is no God besides You in all that we heard with our ears.
verses.7:23: And what other nation on the earth is like Your people Israel, as God guided them to redeem a people for Himself, for You to establish a name, to do greatness and manifestation, for You to drive out from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself out of Egypt, nations and dwellings?
verses.7:24: And You prepared for Yourself Your people Israel as a people forever, and You, Lord, became God to them.
verses.7:25: And now, my Lord, confirm forever the word that You spoke concerning Your servant and his house, Lord Almighty, God of Israel; and now, as You spoke,
verses.7:26: may Your name be magnified forever.
verses.7:27: Lord Almighty, God of Israel, You uncovered the ear of Your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' Therefore Your servant found his heart to pray this prayer to You.
verses.7:28: And now, my Lord, Lord, You are God, and Your words will be true, and You spoke these good things concerning Your servant.
verses.7:29: And now begin and bless the house of Your servant, to be before You forever; for it is You, my Lord, Lord, who spoke, and from the blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever."
verses.8:1: And it happened after these things that David struck the foreigners and routed them; and David took the set-apart territory from the hand of the foreigners.
verses.8:2: And David struck Moab and measured them with cords, having made them lie down on the ground; and the two measured lines were to be put to death, and the two measured lines he kept alive. And Moab became servants to David, bringing gifts.
verses.8:3: And David struck Hadarezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he was going to set his hand upon the river Euphrates.
verses.8:4: And David captured from him one thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers; and David disabled all the chariots, and reserved for himself one hundred chariots.
verses.8:5: And Syria of Damascus came to help Hadarezer king of Zobah, and David struck among the Syrians twenty-two thousand men.
verses.8:6: And David placed a garrison in Syria around Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to David, bringing gifts. And the Lord saved David wherever he went.
verses.8:7: And David took the golden bracelets that he had made upon the servants of Hadarezer king of Zobah, and he brought them to Jerusalem; and Shishak king of Egypt took them when he went up to Jerusalem in the days of Jeroboam son of Solomon.
verses.8:8: And from Masbak, from the choice cities of Hadarezer, King David took very much bronze; with it Solomon made the bronze sea and the pillars and the basins and all the vessels.
verses.8:9: And Tou the king of Hamath heard that David had struck the entire army of Hadarezer,
verses.8:10: and Tou sent his son Jedduran to King David to ask him concerning peace and to bless him because he had struck Hadarezer; and he struck him, for he was opposed to Hadarezer. And in his hands were silver vessels and gold vessels and bronze vessels.
verses.8:11: These also the king consecrated to the Lord, along with the silver and the gold that he had consecrated from all the cities that he had subdued:
verses.8:12: from Idumea, and from the land of Moab, and from the sons of Ammon, and from the foreigners, and from Amalek, and from the spoils of Hadarezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.8:13: And David made a name for himself; and as he was returning, he struck Idumea in Gebelem, up to eighteen thousand.
verses.8:14: And he placed a garrison in Idumea, in all Idumea, and all the Idumeans became servants to the king. And the Lord saved David wherever he went.
verses.8:15: And David reigned over Israel, and he was carrying out justice and righteousness for all his people.
verses.8:16: And Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahijah was over the records,
verses.8:17: and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Asa was the scribe,
verses.8:18: and Benaiah son of Janak was counselor, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; the sons of David were court rulers.
verses.9:1: And David said, "Is there still anyone left of the house of Saul, that I may show mercy to him for the sake of Jonathan?"
verses.9:2: Now from the house of Saul there was a servant, and his name was Ziba, and they called him to David. And the king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he said, "I am your servant."
verses.9:3: And the king said, "Is there still a man left from the house of Saul, that I may show the mercy of God to him?" And Ziba said to the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan, stricken in his feet."
verses.9:4: And the king said, "Where is he?" And Ziba said to the king, "Look, he is in the house of Machir son of Amaer, from Lo-debar."
verses.9:5: And King David sent and took him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
verses.9:6: And Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, came to King David, and fell on his face and bowed down to him. And David said to him, "Mephibosheth." And he said, "Here is your servant."
verses.9:7: And David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will surely show mercy to you for the sake of Jonathan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Saul, the father of your father, and you will eat bread at my table continually."
verses.9:8: And Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "Who am I, your servant, that you have looked upon a dead dog like me?"
verses.9:9: Then the king called Ziba, the attendant of Saul, and said to him, "Everything that belongs to Saul and to all his house I have given to the son of your master.
verses.9:10: And you will work the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and you will bring in bread for the son of your master, and he will eat bread; yet Mephibosheth, the son of your master, will continually eat bread at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.9:11: And Ziba said to the king, "According to everything that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so your servant will do." And Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's own sons.
verses.9:12: And Mephibosheth had a young son, and his name was Micah. And the entire household of Ziba's own house were servants of Mephibosheth.
verses.9:13: And Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, for he ate continually at the king's table. And he was lame in both his feet.
verses.10:1: And it happened after these things that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:2: And David said, "I will show mercy to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed mercy to me." And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father; and the servants of David came into the land of the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:3: And the rulers of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Is it really because David honors your father in your sight that he has sent comforters to you? Rather, has David not sent his servants to you so that they may search the city and spy it out and examine it?"
verses.10:4: And Hanun took the servants of David and shaved their beards and cut off their cloaks in half as far as their hips, and sent them away.
verses.10:5: And they reported to David concerning the men, and he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly dishonored; and the king said, "Remain in Jericho until your beards grow out, and you will return."
verses.10:6: And the sons of Ammon saw that the people of David had been put to shame; and the sons of Ammon sent and hired Syria and Rehob, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Amalek, one thousand men, and Istob, twelve thousand men.
verses.10:7: And David heard, and sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.
verses.10:8: And the sons of Ammon came out and drew up for battle at the entrance of the gate of Syria of Zobah, and Rehob and Istob and Amalek were alone in the field.
verses.10:9: And Joab saw that the battlefront was against him, directly in front and from behind, and he chose from all the young men of Israel, and they drew up opposite Syria.
verses.10:10: And the remainder of the people he gave into the hand of Abishai his brother, and they drew up opposite the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:11: And he said, "If Syria proves stronger than I, then you will be a deliverance for me; and if the sons of Ammon prove stronger than you, then we will be ready to deliver you.
verses.10:12: Be courageous, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God, and the Lord will do what is good in His eyes."
verses.10:13: And Joab and his people with him approached for battle against Syria, and they fled from before him.
verses.10:14: And the sons of Ammon saw that Syria had fled, and they fled from before Abishai and entered the city. And Joab turned back from the sons of Ammon, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.10:15: And Syria saw that it had suffered defeat before Israel, and they gathered together.
verses.10:16: And Hadarezer sent and gathered Syria from beyond the river Chalamak, and they came to Helam; and Shobach, the commander of the army of Hadarezer, was before them.
verses.10:17: And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel, and crossed the Jordan, and they came to Helam; and David drew up opposite Syria, and they fought against him.
verses.10:18: And Syria fled from before Israel; and David destroyed from Syria seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen, and he struck down Shobach the commander of his army, and he died there.
verses.10:19: And all the kings, the servants of Hadarezer, saw that they had suffered defeat before Israel, and they defected to Israel and served them; and Syria was afraid to deliver the sons of Ammon any longer.
verses.11:1: And it happened at the return of the year, at the time of the going out of kings, that David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they destroyed the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah; and David remained in Jerusalem.
verses.11:2: And it happened toward evening that David rose from his bed and was walking on the roof of the king's house; and from the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful in appearance.
verses.11:3: And David sent and inquired about the woman, and someone said, "Is this not Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliab, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?"
verses.11:4: And David sent messengers and took her, and he went in to her and lay with her; and she was purifying herself from her uncleanness; and she returned to her house.
verses.11:5: And the woman conceived, and she sent and reported to David and said, "I am pregnant."
verses.11:6: And David sent to Joab, saying, "Send Uriah the Hittite to me." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.11:7: And Uriah came and went in to him, and David asked about the welfare of Joab and about the welfare of the people and about the welfare of the war.
verses.11:8: And David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." And Uriah went out from the king's house, and a portion from the king went out after him.
verses.11:9: And Uriah slept at the door of the king with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.
verses.11:10: And they reported to David, saying, "Uriah did not go down to his house." And David said to Uriah, "Are you not coming from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?"
verses.11:11: And Uriah said to David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are dwelling in tents, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamping on the face of the field; and shall I go into my house to eat and to drink and to lie with my wife? How? As your soul lives, I will not do this thing."
verses.11:12: And David said to Uriah, "Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away." And Uriah remained in Jerusalem on that day and the next day.
verses.11:13: And David called him, and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk; and in the evening he went out to sleep on his bed with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house.
verses.11:14: And it happened in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
verses.11:15: And he wrote in the letter, saying, "Lead Uriah in opposite the fierce battle, and you will turn back from behind him, and he will be struck and die."
verses.11:16: And it happened, while Joab was keeping watch over the city, that he put Uriah in the place where he knew that men of might were.
verses.11:17: And the men of the city came out and fought against Joab; and some of the people, of the servants of David, fell and died, and Uriah the Hittite also.
verses.11:18: And Joab sent and reported to King David all the matters of the war, to speak to the king.
verses.11:19: And he commanded the messenger, saying, "When you have finished speaking all the matters of the war to the king,
verses.11:20: if it happens that the wrath of the king rises and he says to you, 'Why did you draw near to the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from atop the wall?
verses.11:21: Who struck down Abimelech son of Jeroboam son of Ner? Did not a woman throw a piece of a millstone on him from atop the wall, and he died in Thamasi? Why did you approach the wall?' then you will say, 'Uriah your servant, the Hittite, also died.'"
verses.11:22: And the messenger of Joab went to the king in Jerusalem, and he came and reported to David all that Joab had reported to him, all the matters of the war. And David became angry with Joab, and said to the messenger, "Why did you approach the city to fight? Did you not know that you would be struck from the wall? Who struck down Abimelech son of Jeroboam? Did not a woman throw a piece of a millstone on him from the wall, and he died in Thamasi? Why did you approach the wall?"
verses.11:23: And the messenger said to David, "Because the men prevailed against us and came out against us into the field, and we were upon them as far as the entrance of the gate;
verses.11:24: and the archers shot at your servants from atop the wall, and some of the king's servants died, and your servant Uriah the Hittite also died."
verses.11:25: And David said to the messenger, "Thus you will say to Joab, 'Do not let this thing be evil in your eyes, for the sword devours now in this way and now in that way; strengthen your battle against the city and tear it down.' And strengthen him."
verses.11:26: And the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband had died, and she mourned for her husband.
verses.11:27: And the mourning passed, and David sent and brought her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done appeared evil in the eyes of the Lord.
verses.12:1: And the Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David, and he went in to him and said to him, "There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor.
verses.12:2: And the rich man had very many flocks and herds,
verses.12:3: but the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb, which he acquired and kept alive and raised; and it grew up together with him and with his sons. From his bread it would eat, and from his cup it would drink, and in his bosom it would sleep, and it was to him like a daughter.
verses.12:4: And a traveler came to the rich man, and he held back from taking from his flocks and from his herds to prepare for the traveling guest who had come to him, and he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
verses.12:5: And David grew exceedingly furious with anger against the man, and David said to Nathan, "As the Lord lives, surely the man who did this is a son of death,
verses.12:6: and he shall repay the ewe lamb sevenfold, because he did this thing and because he showed no pity."
verses.12:7: And Nathan said to David, "You are the man who did this! For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: 'I am the One who anointed you as king over Israel, and I am the One who rescued you from the hand of Saul;
verses.12:8: and I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if it is too little, I will add to you according to these things.'
verses.12:9: Because you despised the word of the Lord to do what is evil in His eyes: you struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and you took his wife for yourself as a wife, and him you killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon;
verses.12:10: and now a sword will not depart from your house forever, because you showed contempt and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.
verses.12:11: Thus says the Lord: 'Look, I am raising up evils against you out of your house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
verses.12:12: For you acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and in the sight of this sun.'"
verses.12:13: And David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the Lord." And Nathan said to David, "The Lord also has put away your sin; you will certainly not die.
verses.12:14: However, because you have greatly provoked the enemies of the Lord by this thing, even your son who was born to you will surely die."
verses.12:15: And Nathan departed to his house. And the Lord struck the child whom Uriah's wife bore to David, and he became ill.
verses.12:16: And David sought God concerning the child, and David fasted a fast and went in and spent the night on the ground.
verses.12:17: And the elders of the house stood over him to raise him from the ground, and he was not willing; and he did not eat bread with them.
verses.12:18: And it happened on the seventh day that the child died. And David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "Look, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice; and how can we say to him that the child is dead? And he will do evil things."
verses.12:19: And David perceived that his servants were whispering, and David realized that the child was dead. And David said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said, "He is dead."
verses.12:20: And David arose from the ground, and washed himself and anointed himself and changed his garments, and went into the house of God and worshiped Him; and he went into his house and asked for bread to eat, and they set bread before him, and he ate.
verses.12:21: And his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? For the sake of the child while he was still alive, you were fasting and weeping and staying awake; yet when the child died, you arose and ate bread and have drunk."
verses.12:22: And David said, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, 'Who knows whether the Lord will have mercy on me, and the child will live?'
verses.12:23: But now he is dead; why then am I fasting? Can I bring him back anymore? I will go to him, and he will not return to me."
verses.12:24: And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and he went in to her and lay with her; and she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Solomon, and the Lord loved him.
verses.12:25: And He sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Idedei, for the sake of the Lord.
verses.12:26: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and captured the city of the kingdom.
verses.12:27: And Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the city of the waters;
verses.12:28: and now gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city and capture it first, so that I do not capture the city first and my name be called over it."
verses.12:29: And David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and captured it.
verses.12:30: And he took the crown of Melchol their king from his head, and its weight was a talent of gold and precious stone, and it was on David's head; and he brought out very much plunder of the city.
verses.12:31: And he brought out the people who were in it and set them to the saw and to iron threshing sledges, and led them through the brickworks; and so he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:1: And it happened after these things that Absalom son of David had a sister very beautiful in appearance, and her name was Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
verses.13:2: And Amnon was so distressed that he became ill because of Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin, and it was too difficult in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
verses.13:3: And Amnon had a friend, and his name was Jonadab, son of Shammah, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very wise man.
verses.13:4: And he said to him, "What is the matter with you, that you are so weak, son of the king, morning by morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother."
verses.13:5: And Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and act sick, and your father will come in to see you, and you will say to him, 'Please let Tamar my sister come and feed me, and prepare food before my eyes, so that I may see and eat from her hands.'"
verses.13:6: And Amnon lay down and became ill, and the king came in to see him. And Amnon said to the king, "Please let Tamar my sister come to me and make two cakes before my eyes, and I will eat from her hand."
verses.13:7: And David sent to Tamar at the house, saying, "Please go to your brother's house and prepare food for him."
verses.13:8: And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And she took the dough and kneaded it and made cakes before his eyes, and cooked the cakes.
verses.13:9: And she took the pan and emptied it out before him, but he was not willing to eat. And Amnon said, "Send out every man from before me." And they sent out every man from before him.
verses.13:10: And Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner room, and I will eat from your hand." And Tamar took the cakes that she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother into the bedroom.
verses.13:11: And she brought them near to him to eat, and he seized her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
verses.13:12: And she said to him, "No, my brother, do not humiliate me, for it is not to be done like this in Israel; do not do this folly.
verses.13:13: And as for me, where will I carry my disgrace? And you will be like one of the fools in Israel. And now, please speak to the king, for he will certainly not withhold me from you."
verses.13:14: But Amnon was not willing to listen to her voice, and he overpowered her and humiliated her, and lay with her.
verses.13:15: And Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, for great was the hatred with which he hated her, the last evil greater than the first, beyond the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up and go."
verses.13:16: And Tamar spoke to him concerning this great evil, "Greater than the other that you did with me is sending me away." But Amnon was not willing to listen to her voice.
verses.13:17: And he called his young man who was in charge of the house and said to him, "Please send this one out away from me, and bolt the door behind her."
verses.13:18: Now upon her was a long-sleeved tunic, for in this way the virgin daughters of the king used to wear their outer garments. And his attendant brought her outside and bolted the door behind her.
verses.13:19: And Tamar took ashes and put ashes on her head, and tore the long-sleeved tunic that was on her, and put her hands on her head, and went away, walking and crying out.
verses.13:20: And Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? Now then, my sister, keep silent, for he is your brother; do not set your heart to speak about this matter." And Tamar remained in widowhood in the house of Absalom her brother.
verses.13:21: And King David heard all these matters and grew exceedingly angry; yet he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, because he was his firstborn.
verses.13:22: And Absalom did not speak with Amnon either bad or good, for Absalom hated Amnon on account of the matter that he had humiliated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:23: And it happened after two years of days that there were shearers for Absalom in Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
verses.13:24: And Absalom came to the king and said, "See now, they are shearing for your servant; please let the king and his servants go with your servant."
verses.13:25: And the king said to Absalom, "No, please, my son, let not all of us go, and we will certainly not become a burden on you." And he pressed him, yet he was not willing to go, and he blessed him.
verses.13:26: And Absalom said, "And if not, please let Amnon my brother go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
verses.13:27: But Absalom pressed him, and he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him. And Absalom made a banquet like the banquet of the king.
verses.13:28: And Absalom commanded his young men, saying, "Watch: when Amnon's heart is gladdened with wine and I speak to you, strike down Amnon and put him to death. Do not be afraid, for am I not the one who commands you? Be courageous and be sons of strength."
verses.13:29: And Absalom's young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded them. And all the king's sons arose, and each man mounted his mule, and they fled.
verses.13:30: And it happened while they were on the way that the report came to David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not even one of them has been left."
verses.13:31: And the king arose and tore his garments and lay down on the ground, and all his servants who were standing around him tore their garments.
verses.13:32: And Jonadab son of Shammah, David's brother, answered and said, "Let not my lord the king say that he has put to death all the young men, the king's sons, for Amnon alone has died; for by the mouth of Absalom he was appointed from the day he humiliated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:33: And now let not my lord the king set a word upon his heart, saying, 'All the king's sons have died,' for only Amnon alone has died."
verses.13:34: And Absalom fled away. And the young man, the watchman, lifted up his eyes and saw, and look, many people were coming along the road behind him from the side of the mountain in the descent. And the watchman arrived and reported to the king and said, "I have seen men from the road of Oronen, from the side of the mountain."
verses.13:35: And Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the king's sons are here; according to the word of your servant, so it has happened."
verses.13:36: And it happened when he finished speaking that, look, the king's sons came, and they lifted up their voice and wept; and indeed the king and all his servants wept with a great weeping.
verses.13:37: Now Absalom fled and went to Tholmailem son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, to Machad. And King David mourned for his son all the days.
verses.13:38: And Absalom fled away and went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
verses.13:39: And King David ceased from going out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, because he had died.
verses.14:1: And Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart was toward Absalom.
verses.14:2: And Joab sent to Tekoa, and took from there a wise woman and said to her, "Please mourn, and put on mourning garments, and do not anoint yourself with oil; and you shall be like a woman mourning over one who has died, now for many days,
verses.14:3: and you shall go to the king and speak to him according to this word." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
verses.14:4: And the Tekoite woman went in to the king, and fell on her face to the ground and bowed down to him and said, "Save, king, save!"
verses.14:5: And the king said to her, "What is the matter with you?" And she said, "Truly indeed I am a widow woman, and my husband died.
verses.14:6: And indeed your female servant had two sons, and both of them fought in the field, and there was no one rescuing between them, and the one struck the other, his brother, and put him to death.
verses.14:7: And look, the whole clan has risen up against your female servant and they said, 'Give over the one who struck his brother, and we will put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and we will remove even your heir.' And they will extinguish my coal that is left, so as not to leave for my husband a remnant and a name upon the face of the earth."
verses.14:8: And the king said, "Go in good health to your house, and I myself will give orders concerning you."
verses.14:9: And the Tekoite woman said to the king, "Upon me, my lord the king, be the lawlessness, and upon the house of my father, and the king and his throne are innocent."
verses.14:10: And the king said, "Who is the one speaking to you? And you shall bring him to me, and he will not again touch him."
verses.14:11: And she said, "Please let the king remember the Lord his God, that the kinsman of blood is multiplied to destroy, and they will by no means remove my son." And he said, "As the Lord lives, not a hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
verses.14:12: And she said, "Please let your female servant speak a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."
verses.14:13: And the woman said, "Why have you devised such a thing against the people of God? Or is this word from the mouth of the king like a trespass, in that the king does not bring back his banished one?
verses.14:14: For we will surely die, and are like the water that is wasted upon the ground, which will not be gathered up; and God will take a life, and is devising to banish from Himself a banished one.
verses.14:15: And now, that I have come to speak this word to the king my lord is because the people will see me, and your people will say, 'Please let her speak to the king; perhaps the king will do the word of his female servant,'
verses.14:16: for the king will listen; let him deliver his female servant from the hand of the man seeking to remove me and my son from the inheritance of God."
verses.14:17: And the woman said, "Please let the word of my lord the king be for sacrifices, for just as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to hear the good and the evil; and the Lord your God will be with you."
verses.14:18: And the king answered and said to the woman, "Please do not hide from me a word that I am asking you." And the woman said, "Please let my lord the king speak."
verses.14:19: And the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" And the woman said to the king, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, there is nothing to the right or to the left from all that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab himself commanded me, and he himself put all these words in the mouth of your female servant,
verses.14:20: in order to turn around the face of this matter which your servant Joab has done, this deceit. And my lord is wise, like the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are in the earth."
verses.14:21: And the king said to Joab, "Look now, I have done for you according to this word of yours; bring back the young man Absalom."
verses.14:22: And Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed down and blessed the king; and Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because my lord the king has done the word of his servant."
verses.14:23: And Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.14:24: And the king said, "Let him turn back to his house, and let him not see my face." And Absalom turned back to his house, and he did not see the king's face.
verses.14:25: And like Absalom there was no man in all Israel so exceedingly praiseworthy; from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
verses.14:26: And when he sheared his head, and it happened from the beginning of days to days whenever he sheared it, because it grew heavy upon him, then shearing it, he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the royal shekel.
verses.14:27: And to Absalom were born three sons and one daughter, and her name was Tamar; she was a very beautiful woman, and she became wife to Rehoboam son of Solomon and bore to him Abiathar.
verses.14:28: And Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years of days, and he did not see the king's face.
verses.14:29: And Absalom sent to Joab to send him to the king, and he was not willing to come to him; and he sent a second time to him, and he was not willing to come.
verses.14:30: And Absalom said to his servants, "See, Joab's portion in the field is next to mine, and he has barley there; go and burn it with fire." And Absalom's servants burned it, the portion. And Joab's servants came to him with their garments torn and said, "Absalom's servants have burned the portion with fire."
verses.14:31: And Joab arose and came to Absalom at the house, and said to him, "Why have your servants burned my portion with fire?"
verses.14:32: And Absalom said to Joab, "Look, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, and I will send you to the king, saying, "Why did I come from Geshur? It was good for me to be there."' And now, look, I have not seen the king's face; and if there is unrighteousness in me, then put me to death."
verses.14:33: And Joab went in to the king and reported to him, and he called Absalom. And he went in to the king and bowed down to him, and fell on his face to the ground and before the face of the king. And the king kissed Absalom.
verses.15:1: And it happened after these things that Absalom made for himself chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.15:2: And Absalom rose early in the morning and stood beside the way of the gate; and it happened that every man who had a case came to the king for judgment, and Absalom called out to him and would say to him, "From what city are you?" And he said, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.15:3: And Absalom said to him, "Look, your words are good and straightforward, and there is no one from the king listening to you."
verses.15:4: And Absalom said, "Who will appoint me judge in the land, so that every man who has a dispute and a case will come to me, and I will give him justice?"
verses.15:5: And it happened when a man came near to bow down to him, that he stretched out his hand and took hold of him and kissed him.
verses.15:6: And Absalom did according to this matter to all Israel who came to the king for judgment, and Absalom made the heart of the men of Israel his own.
verses.15:7: And it happened at the end of forty years that Absalom said to his father, "Please let me go and pay my vows which I vowed to the Lord in Hebron;
verses.15:8: for your servant vowed a vow while I was living in Geshur in Syria, saying, 'If the Lord indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.'"
verses.15:9: And the king said to him, "Go in peace." And he arose and went to Hebron.
verses.15:10: And Absalom sent spies among all the tribes of Israel, saying, "When you hear the sound of the horn, then you shall say, 'King Absalom is reigning in Hebron!'"
verses.15:11: And with Absalom went two hundred men from Jerusalem who were invited; and they went in their innocence and did not know anything.
verses.15:12: And Absalom sent to Ahithophel the Tekonite, the counselor of David, in his city, to Gola, while he was offering sacrifices. And there was a severe shattering, and the people going along were also numerous with Absalom.
verses.15:13: And the messenger arrived to David, saying, "The heart of the men of Israel has gone after Absalom."
verses.15:14: And David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Arise and let us flee, for there is no deliverance for us from the face of Absalom; hurry to go, so that he may not hurry and overtake us, and thrust evil upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.15:15: And the servants of the king said to the king, "According to everything that our lord the king chooses, look, here are your servants."
verses.15:16: And the king went out, and all his household on foot; and the king left ten women of his concubines to guard the house.
verses.15:17: And the king went out, and all his servants on foot, and they stood at the Far House.
verses.15:18: And all his servants were passing by beside him, and all the Chettites and all the Pelethites, and they stood at the olive tree in the wilderness; and all the people were passing by next to him, and all those around him and all the prominent men and all the warriors, six hundred men, and they were present beside him; and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites and all the Gittites, the six hundred men who came on foot to Gath and were going before the face of the king.
verses.15:19: And the king said to Seththi the Gittite, "Why are you also going with us? Return and live with the king, for you are a foreigner and because you have migrated from your place.
verses.15:20: If you arrived yesterday, shall I today move you with us? And indeed you will leave your place; yesterday was your coming out, and today shall I make you move away to go with us? And I will go wherever I may go; return, and bring back your brothers with you, and the Lord will do mercy and truth with you."
verses.15:21: And Ittai answered the king and said, "As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in the place wherever my lord may be, whether for death or for life, surely there your servant will be."
verses.15:22: And the king said to Seththi, "Come and cross over with me." And Seththi the Gittite passed over, and all his servants and all the crowd that was with him.
verses.15:23: And all the land was weeping with a loud voice; and all the people were passing along in the brook of the cedars, and the king crossed the brook Kidron; and all the people and the king were passing along facing the road to the wilderness.
verses.15:24: And look, Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, were carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Baithar. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up when all the people finished passing out of the city.
verses.15:25: And the king said to Zadok, "Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, then He will bring me back and show me it and its beauty;
verses.15:26: and if He says thus, 'I have no delight in you,' look, here I am; let Him do to me according to what is good in His eyes."
verses.15:27: And the king said to Zadok the priest, "See, you are returning to the city in peace, and Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, your two sons, with you.
verses.15:28: See, I am campaigning in Araboth of the wilderness until a word comes from you to report to me."
verses.15:29: And Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark to Jerusalem and remained there.
verses.15:30: And David was going up by the ascent of the olive trees and with his head covered, and he himself was walking barefoot; and all the people who were with him, each man covered his head, and they were going up, ascending and weeping.
verses.15:31: And it was reported to David, saying, "Ahithophel also is among those conspiring with Absalom." And David said, "Please frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel, Lord my God."
verses.15:32: And David was coming as far as Roos, where he worshiped God there; and look, coming to meet him was Hushai the Archite, the friend of David, with his tunic torn and earth on his head.
verses.15:33: And David said to him, "If you cross over with me, then you will be a burden upon me.
verses.15:34: But if you return to the city, and you say to Absalom, 'Your brothers have passed on, and the king, your father, has passed on behind me; and now I am your servant, king, let me live; I was your father's servant then and just now, and now I am your servant,' then you will frustrate for me the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.15:35: And look, with you there are Zadok and Abiathar the priests. And it shall be that every word that you hear from the king's house, you shall report to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.15:36: Look, there with them are their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar; and you shall send by their hand to me every word that you hear."
verses.15:37: And Hushai the friend of David went into the city, and Absalom was entering Jerusalem.
verses.16:1: And David passed a little way beyond Roos, and look, Ziba, the attendant of Mephibosheth, was there to meet him with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them were two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred clusters of raisins, one hundred dates, and a skin of wine.
verses.16:2: And the king said to Ziba, "What do you have these for?" And Ziba said, "The pack animals are for the household of the king to ride on, and the loaves of bread and the dates are for food for the attendants, and the wine is to drink for those who are exhausted in the wilderness."
verses.16:3: And the king said, "And where is the son of your lord?" And Ziba said to the king, "Look, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will return to me the kingdom of my father.'"
verses.16:4: And the king said to Ziba, "Look, everything that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." And Ziba said, "Bowing down, may I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."
verses.16:5: And King David came as far as Bahurim; and look, a man was coming out from there, from the clan of the house of Saul, and his name was Shimei, the son of Gera; he came out, walking along and cursing,
verses.16:6: and throwing stones at David and at all the servants of King David; and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right and on the left of the king.
verses.16:7: And Shimei was saying this as he cursed: "Get out, get out, man of bloodshed and lawless man!
verses.16:8: The Lord has returned upon you all the bloodshed of the house of Saul, because you reigned in his place, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. And look, you are in your calamity, because you are a man of bloodshed."
verses.16:9: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why is this dead dog cursing my lord the king? Let me go over now and take off his head."
verses.16:10: And the king said, "What do I have to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Leave him alone, and let him curse like this, because the Lord told him to curse David; and who will say, 'Why have you done so?'"
verses.16:11: And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Look, my own son who came out from my body seeks my life, and now in addition the son of the Jeminite! Leave him alone to curse, because the Lord has told him to;
verses.16:12: perhaps the Lord will look upon my humiliation, and He will return good to me in place of his curse on this day."
verses.16:13: And David and his men went along the road; and Shimei kept going along the side of the mountain next to him, going along and cursing, and throwing stones from beside him and scattering dust.
verses.16:14: And the king and all his people arrived exhausted, and they refreshed themselves there.
verses.16:15: And Absalom and all the men of Israel entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
verses.16:16: And it happened when Hushai the Archite, the friend of David, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king!"
verses.16:17: And Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your mercy toward your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
verses.16:18: And Hushai said to Absalom, "No, but following the one whom the Lord and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, to him I will belong, and with him I will stay.
verses.16:19: And secondly, whom will I serve? Is it not before his son? Just as I served before your father, so I will be before you."
verses.16:20: And Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give counsel among yourselves as to what we should do."
verses.16:21: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to the concubines of your father, whom he left behind to guard the house, and all Israel will hear that you have disgraced your father, and the hands of all who are with you will grow strong."
verses.16:22: And they pitched the tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines before the eyes of all Israel.
verses.16:23: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he gave in the former days, was just as when one inquires by the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both for David and for Absalom.
verses.17:1: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose for myself now twelve thousand men, and I will rise up and pursue after David tonight.
verses.17:2: And I will come upon him while he is weary and weakened in his hands, and I will throw him into panic, and all the people who are with him will flee, and I will strike down the king all alone;
verses.17:3: and I will return all the people to you, just as a bride returns to her husband; only you are seeking the life of one man, and for all the people there will be peace."
verses.17:4: And the word was right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.
verses.17:5: And Absalom said, "Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear what is in his mouth as well."
verses.17:6: And Hushai went in to Absalom; and Absalom spoke to him, saying, "It is according to this word that Ahithophel has spoken; should we act according to his word? If not, you speak."
verses.17:7: And Hushai said to Absalom, "This counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good."
verses.17:8: And Hushai said, "You know your father and his men, that they are very mighty and deeply bitter in their soul, like a bear robbed of her cubs in a field and like a fierce sow in the plain. And your father is a warrior, and he will certainly not let the people rest.
verses.17:9: For look, he is now hidden in one of the hills or in one of the places; and it will happen, when he falls upon them at the start, that whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom,'
verses.17:10: then even he, a son of strength, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will completely melt; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and those who are with him are sons of strength.
verses.17:11: For thus I myself firmly counsel: all Israel will surely be gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand that is by the sea in multitude, and your own presence going in their midst;
verses.17:12: and we will come to him in one of the places where we may find him, and we will encamp upon him as the dew falls on the earth, and of him and the men who are with him we will not leave even one.
verses.17:13: And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel will take ropes to that city, and we will drag it all the way into the brook, so that not even a stone will be left there."
verses.17:14: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the good counsel of Ahithophel." And the Lord had commanded to thwart the counsel of Ahithophel, so that the Lord might bring upon Absalom all the evil.
verses.17:15: And Hushai the Archite said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "Thus and thus Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I counseled.
verses.17:16: And now send quickly and report to David, saying, 'Do not spend the night tonight in Araboth of the wilderness, but indeed hurry to cross over, so that he may not persuade the king and all the people who are with him.'"
verses.17:17: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were standing at the spring of Rogel, and the servant girl went and reported to them; and they were to go and report to King David, for they could not be seen entering the city.
verses.17:18: And a boy saw them, and they reported to Absalom; so the two of them went quickly and entered the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a cistern in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
verses.17:19: And the woman took and spread the covering over the opening of the cistern and dried araphoth on it, and nothing became known.
verses.17:20: And the servants of Absalom came to the woman at the house and said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman said to them, "They went a little past the water." And they searched and did not find them, and they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.17:21: Now it happened after they departed that they came up out of the cistern, and they went and reported to King David, and said to David, "Rise up and cross the water quickly, for Ahithophel has counseled thus concerning you."
verses.17:22: And David and all the people who were with him rose up and crossed the Jordan until the light of morning; not even one was missing who had not passed over the Jordan.
verses.17:23: And Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not carried out, and he saddled his donkey and rose up and went away to his house, to his city; and he gave orders to his household, and he hanged himself and died, and he was buried in the tomb of his father.
verses.17:24: And David went on to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.17:25: And Absalom appointed Amasa in place of Joab over the army; and Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Jether the Israelite, who went in to Abigail, the daughter of Nahash, brother of Zeruiah, mother of Joab.
verses.17:26: And all Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
verses.17:27: And it happened when David came to Mahanaim, Ouesbei the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,
verses.17:28: brought ten beds, and double-sided rugs, and ten basins, and earthenware vessels, and wheat and barley, and flour and barley meal, and beans and lentils,
