verses.17:29: and honey and butter, and sheep and sapphoth of cattle; and they presented them to David and to the people who were with him to eat, for he said, "The people are hungry and exhausted and thirsty in the wilderness."
verses.18:1: And David inspected the people who were with him, and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.
verses.18:2: And David sent out the people: a third under the hand of Joab, and a third under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, and a third under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And David said to the people, "I myself will also surely go out with you."
verses.18:3: And they said, "You must not go out, for if we indeed flee, they will not pay attention to us, and if half of us die, they will not pay attention to us, for you are like ten thousand of us; and now it is good that you will be a help to us in the city to give help."
verses.18:4: And the king said to them, "Whatever is pleasing in your eyes I will do." And the king stood beside the gate, and all the people were going out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.18:5: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, "Spare for my sake the young man Absalom." And all the people heard the king commanding all the commanders concerning Absalom.
verses.18:6: And all the people went out into the forest against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
verses.18:7: And the people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and the slaughter was great on that day, twenty thousand men.
verses.18:8: And the battle there became spread out over the face of all the land, and the forest devoured more from among the people than those whom the sword devoured among the people on that day.
verses.18:9: And Absalom came face to face with the servants of David; and Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the dense branches of the great oak, and his head was suspended in the oak, and he was suspended between heaven and earth, and the mule beneath him passed on.
verses.18:10: And one man saw it and reported to Joab, and said, "Look, I have seen Absalom hanging in the oak."
verses.18:11: And Joab said to the man reporting it, "And look, you have seen him! Why did you not strike him to the ground? And I would have given you ten pieces of silver and one belt."
verses.18:12: But the man said to Joab, "Though I am weighing out a thousand shekels of silver into my hands, I will by no means lay my hand on the king's son; for in our ears the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, 'Guard for me the young man Absalom,
verses.18:13: so as not to do wrong against his life.' And no matter will be hidden from the king, and you yourself will stand in opposition."
verses.18:14: And Joab said, "This I will begin; I will not wait like this before you." And Joab took three darts in his hand, and they thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.
verses.18:15: And ten young men carrying Joab's armor circled around, and they struck Absalom and put him to death.
verses.18:16: And Joab sounded a horn, and the people turned back from pursuing Israel, for Joab was sparing the people.
verses.18:17: And he took Absalom and threw him into a great chasm in the forest, into the great pit, and erected over him a very great heap of stones; and all Israel fled, each man to his tent.
verses.18:18: Now Absalom, while still alive, had set up for himself the pillar in which he was taken and erected it to take, the pillar that is in the Valley of the King; for he said that he had no son to keep his name in remembrance, and he called the pillar Hand of Absalom to this day.
verses.18:19: And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, "Please let me run and bring good news to the king that the Lord has rendered judgment from the hand of his enemies."
verses.18:20: And Joab said to him, "You are not a man of good news on this day, and you will bring good news on another day; but on this day you will not bring good news, because the king's son has died."
verses.18:21: And Joab said to Cushi, "Go, report to the king all that you have seen." And Cushi bowed down to Joab and went out.
verses.18:22: And Ahimaaz the son of Zadok continued further and said to Joab, "And let it be that I also run after Cushi." And Joab said, "Why is it that you are running, my son? Come, you have no good news for profit as you go."
verses.18:23: And he said, "For what if I run?" And Joab said to him, "Run." And Ahimaaz ran by the way of Kechar and passed Cushi.
verses.18:24: And David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman went to the roof of the gate by the wall, and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and see, a man was running alone before him.
verses.18:25: And the watchman cried out and reported to the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, good news is in his mouth." And he kept coming on and drawing near.
verses.18:26: And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called out at the gate and said, "Look, another man running alone!" And the king said, "This one also is bringing good news."
verses.18:27: And the watchman said, "I see the running of the first as the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said, "This is a good man, and he also will come with good news."
verses.18:28: And Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, "Peace!" And he bowed down to the king with his face to the ground and said, "Blessed is the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men who hate their hand against my lord the king."
verses.18:29: And the king said, "Is there peace for the young man Absalom?" And Ahimaaz said, "I saw the great crowd when Joab sent the king's servant and your servant, and I did not know what was there."
verses.18:30: And the king said, "Turn aside, take your stand here." And he turned aside and stood.
verses.18:31: And look, Cushi arrived and said to the king, "Let my lord the king receive good news, for the Lord has rendered judgment for you today from the hand of all those rising up against you."
verses.18:32: And the king said to Cushi, "Is there peace for the young man Absalom?" And Cushi said, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rose up against him for evil, become like the young man."
verses.19:1: And the king was troubled, and he went up to the upper chamber of the gate and wept. And thus he said as he went, "My son, my son, Absalom! Who would grant my death in place of you? I in place of you, Absalom, my son, my son!"
verses.19:2: And it was reported to Joab, saying, "Look, the king is weeping and mourning over Absalom."
verses.19:3: And the deliverance on that day turned into mourning for all the people, because the people heard on that day, saying, "The king is grieved over his son."
verses.19:4: And the people were creeping stealthily on that day to enter the city, just as people who are ashamed creep stealthily when they flee in battle.
verses.19:5: And the king hid his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, saying, "My son Absalom, Absalom, my son!"
verses.19:6: And Joab went in to the king into the house and said, "You have put to shame today the face of all your servants who rescued you today, and the life of your sons and of your daughters, and the life of your wives and of your concubines,
verses.19:7: by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you; and you have declared today that your commanders and servants are nothing, for I know today that if Absalom were alive, all of us dead today, then that would have been right in your eyes.
verses.19:8: And now arise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants, for I have sworn by the Lord that if you do not go out today, not a man will lodge with you this night; and know for yourself: this will be evil for you beyond all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now."
verses.19:9: And the king arose and sat in the gate, and all the people reported, saying, "Look, the king is sitting in the gate." And all the people came in before the king. And Israel had fled, each man to his tents.
verses.19:10: And all the people were disputing throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "King David delivered us from the hand, from all our enemies, and he himself rescued us from the hand of foreigners; and now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom and from Absalom.
verses.19:11: The one whom we anointed over us died in battle. And now why are you keeping silent about returning to the king?" And the word of all Israel came to the king.
verses.19:12: And King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why are you becoming the last to return to the king to his house? And the word of all Israel has come to the king.
verses.19:13: You are brothers to me; you are my bones and my flesh. Why are you becoming the last to bring back the king to his house?'
verses.19:14: And to Amasa you shall say, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? And now may God do so to me, and so also may He add, if you will not be commander of the army before me all the days in place of Joab.'"
verses.19:15: And he inclined the heart of all the men of Judah, even to one man; and they sent to the king, saying, "Return, you and all your servants."
verses.19:16: And the king returned and came as far as the Jordan; and the men of Judah came to Gilgal to go to meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.
verses.19:17: And Shimei son of Gera, son of the Jeminite, from Bahurim hurried and went down with the men of Judah to meet King David,
verses.19:18: and a thousand men of Benjamin were with him, and Ziba the attendant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons with him and his twenty servants with him; and they made straight for the Jordan before the king,
verses.19:19: and they performed the service of bringing the king across; and the ferry crossed over to rouse the house of the king and to do what was right in his eyes. And Shimei son of Gera fell on his face before the king as he was crossing the Jordan,
verses.19:20: and said to the king, "May my lord not reckon lawlessness, and do not remember all the wrong your servant did on the day when my lord was going out from Jerusalem, for the king to lay it to his heart;
verses.19:21: for your servant knows that I have sinned, and look, I have come today first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king."
verses.19:22: And Abishai son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Should Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of the Lord?"
verses.19:23: And David said, "What do I have to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you are becoming an adversary to me today? Today no man from Israel shall be put to death; for do I not know whether today I reign over Israel?"
verses.19:24: And the king said to Shimei, "You shall certainly not die." And the king swore to him.
verses.19:25: And Mephibosheth, the son of the son of Saul, went down to meet the king; and he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his nails, nor groomed his mustache, and he had not washed his garments from the day the king departed until the day he himself arrived in peace.
verses.19:26: And it happened, when he entered Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, "Why is it that you did not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
verses.19:27: And Mephibosheth said to him, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me; for your servant said to him, 'Saddle the donkey for me so that I may mount her and go with the king,' because your servant is lame.
verses.19:28: And he schemed against your servant to my lord the king; and my lord the king did what is good openly, like an angel of God. And do what is good in your eyes;
verses.19:29: for all the house of my father was nothing except men of death to my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. And what just claim do I still have, even to cry out any longer to the king?"
verses.19:30: And the king said to him, "Why do you still speak your words? I have said, 'You and Ziba shall divide the field.'"
verses.19:31: And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him even take everything, after my lord the king has arrived in peace at his house."
verses.19:32: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed the Jordan with the king to escort him across the Jordan.
verses.19:33: And Barzillai was a very old man, eighty years old; and he himself had provided for the king while he lived in Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.
verses.19:34: And the king said to Barzillai, "You shall cross over with me, and I will provide for your old age with me in Jerusalem."
verses.19:35: And Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
verses.19:36: I am eighty years old today. Can I indeed discern between good and bad, to evil? Will your servant still taste what I will eat or drink? Or will I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why should your servant still be a burden upon my lord the king?
verses.19:37: Your servant will cross the Jordan just a short way with the king; and why is the king rewarding me with this reward?
verses.19:38: Please let your servant stay, and I will die in my city, beside the tomb of my father and of my mother. And look, your servant Chimham will cross over with my lord the king; and do for him what is good in your eyes."
verses.19:39: And the king said, "Let Chimham cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes, and all that you choose of me I will do for you."
verses.19:40: And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed over; and the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his place.
verses.19:41: And the king crossed over to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him; and all the people of Judah were crossing over with the king, and also half of the people of Israel.
verses.19:42: And look, all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why is it that our brothers, the men of Judah, have stolen you away, and have brought the king and his house across the Jordan, and all the men of David with him?"
verses.19:43: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel and said, "Because the king is close to me? And why have you become so angry about this matter? Have we eaten at all from the king, or has he given a gift, or lifted a portion for us?"
verses.19:44: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, "I have ten shares in the king, and I am firstborn rather than you, and indeed I am in David more than you. And why have you insulted me like this, and was my word not reckoned first for me ahead of Judah, to bring back the king for me?" And the word of the men of Judah was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.
verses.20:1: And there was one called a lawless man, and his name was Sheba son of Bichri, a Jeminite man; and he blew the horn and said, "We have no portion in David, nor do we have an inheritance in the son of Jesse! Each man to your tents, Israel!"
verses.20:2: And all Israel went up from behind David, after Sheba son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clung to their king from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.
verses.20:3: And David went into his house in Jerusalem. And the king took the ten women, his concubines, whom he had left to guard the house, and put them in a house under guard, and he provided for them, yet he did not go in to them. And they were confined until the day of their death, living widows.
verses.20:4: And the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah for me within three days, and you stand here."
verses.20:5: And Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the time that he had appointed for him.
verses.20:6: And David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom; and now you take with yourself the servants of your lord and pursue after him, so that he may not find fortified cities for himself and overshadow our eyes."
verses.20:7: And Abishai went out after him, and the men of Joab, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.
verses.20:8: And they were beside the great stone that is in Gibeon, and Amasa came in front of them. And Joab was belted in a cloak, his garment, and over it he was belted with a sword fastened upon his waist in its sheath; and the sword came out, and it came out and fell.
verses.20:9: And Joab said to Amasa, "Are you well, brother?" And the right hand of Joab took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.
verses.20:10: And Amasa was not on guard against the sword that was in Joab's hand; and Joab struck him with it in the abdomen, and his entrails poured out onto the ground, and he did not strike him a second time, and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba son of Bichri.
verses.20:11: And a man from Joab's attendants stood over him and said, "Who favors Joab, and who is for David? After Joab!"
verses.20:12: And Amasa was drenched in blood in the middle of the road, and a man saw that all the people were standing still; and they removed Amasa from the road into a field, and he threw a garment over him, because he saw everyone who came up to him standing still.
verses.20:13: And when he was gone from the road, all the men of Israel passed on after Joab to pursue after Sheba son of Bichri.
verses.20:14: And he passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and to Beth-maacah, and all in Charri, and they were assembled; and he came after him.
verses.20:15: And they arrived and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah, and they cast up a siege mound against the city, and it stood at the outer wall; and all the people who were with Joab were planning to throw down the wall.
verses.20:16: And a wise woman cried out from the wall and said, "Listen, listen! Please say to Joab, 'Come near to here,' and I will speak to him."
verses.20:17: And he came near to her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" And he said, "I am." And she said to him, "Listen to the words of your maidservant." And Joab said, "I myself am listening."
verses.20:18: And she spoke, saying, "They spoke a saying in former times, saying, 'Surely one was asked in Abel and in Dan whether the things that the faithful of Israel established had failed; they will surely inquire of one in Abel, and so, whether they failed.'
verses.20:19: I am peaceful among the supports of Israel, yet you seek to put to death a city and a mother city in Israel. Why are you engulfing the inheritance of the Lord?"
verses.20:20: And Joab answered and said, "Far be it from me, far be it from me, that I should engulf or that I should destroy!
verses.20:21: This is not the matter; for a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against King David. Give him to me alone, and I will depart away from the city." And the woman said to Joab, "Look, his head will be thrown to you through the wall."
verses.20:22: And the woman went in to all the people, and she spoke to all the city in her wisdom; and she cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri, and took it away and threw it to Joab. And he blew the horn, and they dispersed from the city, away from him, each man to his tents. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
verses.20:23: And Joab was over all the army of Israel, and Benaiah son of Ahilud was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites,
verses.20:24: and Adoniram was over the tribute, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder,
verses.20:25: and Joshua was the scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests,
verses.20:26: and Ira the Jairite was also a priest of David.
verses.21:1: And there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year, and David sought the face of the Lord. And the Lord said, "Upon Saul and upon his house is injustice on account of him, by a death of bloodshed, because he put the Gibeonites to death."
verses.21:2: And King David called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites are not sons of Israel, but rather from the blood of the Amorites, and the sons of Israel swore to them; and Saul sought to strike them down in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah.
verses.21:3: And David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you, and with what shall I make atonement, so that you will bless the inheritance of the Lord?"
verses.21:4: And the Gibeonites said to him, "There is no silver and gold for us with Saul and with his house, and there is no man for us to put to death in Israel." And he said, "What do you say, and I will do it for you?"
verses.21:5: And they said to the king, "The man brought destruction upon us and pursued us, who schemed to utterly destroy us; let us wipe him out so that he may not stand in any territory of Israel.
verses.21:6: Let him give us seven men from his sons, and let us expose them in the sun to the Lord in Gibeon of Saul, chosen ones of the Lord." And the king said, "I will give them."
verses.21:7: And the king spared Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath of the Lord that was between them, even between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
verses.21:8: And the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Serei the son of Barzillai the Meholathite,
verses.21:9: and he gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites. And they exposed them in the sun on the mountain before the Lord, and the seven of them fell together. And they were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.21:10: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and pitched it for herself by the rock at the beginning of the barley harvest until water dripped upon them from the sky, and she did not allow the birds of the sky to rest upon them by day nor the wild beasts of the field by night.
verses.21:11: And it was reported to David all that Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done; and they grew faint, and Dan the son of Joa, from the descendants of the giants, overtook them.
verses.21:12: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men, the sons of Jabesh-gilead, who stole them from the open square of Beth, because the foreigners had set them up there on the day when the foreigners struck down Saul in Gilboa.
verses.21:13: And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and he gathered the bones of those exposed in the sun.
verses.21:14: And they buried the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and of those exposed in the sun who were in the land of Benjamin, in the side, in the tomb of Kish his father. And they did all that the king commanded, and God listened to the land after these things.
verses.21:15: And there was again war for the foreigners with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought with the foreigners, and David departed.
verses.21:16: And Ishbi, who was among the offspring of Rapha—and the weight of his spear was three hundred shekels of bronze by weight, and he was girded with a club—intended to strike down David.
verses.21:17: And Abishai the son of Zeruiah helped him, and struck down the foreigner and put him to death. Then the men of David swore, saying, "You shall not go out with us to war anymore, and you shall by no means extinguish the lamp of Israel."
verses.21:18: And after these things there was again war in Gath with the foreigners; then Oebocha the Hastatothite struck down Saph, who was among the offspring of Rapha.
verses.21:19: And the war took place in Rom with the foreigners; and Elhanan the son of Ariorgim the Bethlehemite struck down Godolias the Hittite, and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam.
verses.21:20: And there was again war in Gath; and there was a man of Madon, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number; and he also was born to Rapha.
verses.21:21: And he taunted Israel, and Jonathan the son of Shimei, the brother of David, struck him down.
verses.21:22: These four were born descendants of the giants in Gath, a house for Rapha, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
verses.22:1: And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song on the day when the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
verses.22:2: And he said: A song. "Lord, my rock and my stronghold, and the One who delivers me for myself.
verses.22:3: My God will be my guardian; I will trust in Him, my defender and the horn of my salvation, my supporter and my refuge of my salvation; from injustice You will save me.
verses.22:4: I will call upon the praiseworthy Lord, and from my enemies I will be saved.
verses.22:5: For crushings of death encompassed me; torrents of lawlessness terrified me;
verses.22:6: pangs of death surrounded me; severities of death confronted me.
verses.22:7: In my distress I will call upon the Lord, and to my God I will cry out; and He will hear my voice from His temple, and my cry will be in His ears.
verses.22:8: And the earth was agitated and shaken, and the foundations of heaven were thrown into turmoil and were convulsed, because the Lord was angry with them.
verses.22:9: Smoke went up in His wrath, and fire from His mouth will devour; coals were kindled from Him.
verses.22:10: And He bent the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was beneath His feet.
verses.22:11: And He sat upon cherubim and flew, and He appeared upon the wings of the wind.
verses.22:12: And He set the darkness of His hiding place around Him; His tent was darkness of waters; He thickened it in clouds of air.
verses.22:13: From the brightness before Him, coals of fire were kindled.
verses.22:14: The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice;
verses.22:15: and He sent arrows and scattered them, lightning, and confounded them.
verses.22:16: And the channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered at the rebuke of the Lord, from the blast of the breath of His fury.
verses.22:17: He sent from on high and took me; He pulled me out of many waters.
verses.22:18: He rescued me from my strong enemies, from those who hate me, for they became stronger than me.
verses.22:19: The days of my distress confronted me, and the Lord became my support;
verses.22:20: and He brought me out into a broad place, and He delivered me, because He delighted in me.
verses.22:21: And the Lord repaid me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands He repaid me.
verses.22:22: For I kept the ways of the Lord, and I did not act impiously away from my God;
verses.22:23: for all His judgments were before me, and as for His ordinances, I did not turn away from them.
verses.22:24: And I will be blameless before Him, and I will guard myself from my lawlessness;
verses.22:25: and the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before His eyes.
verses.22:26: With a devout one You will show Yourself devout, and with a perfect man You will show Yourself perfect;
verses.22:27: and with a chosen one You will be chosen, and with a crooked one You will show Yourself crooked.
verses.22:28: And the poor people You will save, and eyes upon the lofty You will humble.
verses.22:29: For You are my lamp, Lord, and the Lord will illuminate my darkness for me.
verses.22:30: For by You I will run lightly armed, and by my God I will scale a wall.
verses.22:31: As for the Mighty One, His way is blameless; the word of the Lord is strong, refined by fire; He is a defender to all those who trust in Him.
verses.22:32: Who is mighty except the Lord? And who will be a creator except our God?
verses.22:33: The Mighty One is the One who strengthens me with power, and He shook out my way blameless,
verses.22:34: making my feet like those of deer, and setting me upon the heights,
verses.22:35: teaching my hands for war, and breaking a bronze bow with my arm.
verses.22:36: And You gave me the defense of my salvation, and Your listening multiplied me, into a broad place for my steps beneath me,
verses.22:37: and my legs were not shaken.
verses.22:38: I will pursue my enemies and wipe them out, and I will not turn back until I bring them to an end;
verses.22:39: and I will crush them, and they will not rise, and they will fall under my feet.
verses.22:40: And You will strengthen me with power for war; You will bend down those who rise up against me beneath me.
verses.22:41: And You gave me the back of my enemies, those who hate me, and You put them to death.
verses.22:42: They will cry out, and there is no helper; to the Lord, and He did not listen to them.
verses.22:43: And I ground them fine like dust of the earth; like mud of the streets I pulverized them.
verses.22:44: And You will rescue me from the strife of peoples; You will keep me as head of nations. A people whom I did not know served me;
verses.22:45: foreign sons lied to me; at the hearing of the ear they obeyed me;
verses.22:46: foreign sons will be cast away and will stumble out of their enclosures.
verses.22:47: The Lord lives, and blessed is my guardian, and my God, the guardian of my salvation, will be exalted.
verses.22:48: Mighty is the Lord, who gives acts of vengeance to me, disciplining peoples beneath me,
verses.22:49: and bringing me out from my enemies; and from those who rise up against me You will lift me up; from a man of wrongdoings You will rescue me.
verses.22:50: Therefore I will give thanks to You, Lord, among the nations, and in Your name I will sing praise.
verses.22:51: He magnifies the acts of salvation of His king and shows mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed forever." And these are the last words of David.
verses.23:1: Faithful is David son of Jesse, and faithful is the man whom the Lord raised up over the anointed of the God of Jacob, and lovely are the psalms of Israel.
verses.23:2: The Spirit of the Lord spoke in me, and His word was upon my tongue.
verses.23:3: The God of Israel says; the Guardian from Israel spoke to me, "Speak a parable: 'In man, how may you strengthen the fear of the anointed?
verses.23:4: And in God, the light of morning, may the sun rise; in the morning the Lord did not pass by from brightness, and as from rain of fresh grass from the earth.'"
verses.23:5: For is not this my house with the Mighty One? For He established an eternal covenant with me, prepared at every time, guarded; for it is all my salvation and every desire; for the lawless one will by no means sprout.
verses.23:6: Like a thorn thrust away are all these, for they will not be taken by hand.
verses.23:7: And a man will not toil among them; and it is full of iron and the shaft of a spear, and in fire it will burn, and they will set their shame.
verses.23:8: These are the names of the mighty men of David: Jebosthe the Canaanite is commander of the third; Adinon the Asonite, he drew his sword against eight hundred soldiers at one time.
verses.23:9: And after him was Elhanan son of his uncle, son of Susi, who was among the three mighty men with David; and when he taunted among the foreigners, they were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel cried out.
verses.23:10: He arose and struck among the foreigners until his hand grew weary, and his hand clung to the sword; and the Lord brought about a great salvation on that day, and the people sat behind him only to strip them.
verses.23:11: And after him was Samaia son of Asa, the Aruchite; and the foreigners were gathered at Theria, and there was a plot of the field there full of lentils, and the people fled from before the foreigners.
verses.23:12: And he stood firm in the middle of the plot, and rescued it and struck the foreigners, and the Lord brought about a great salvation.
verses.23:13: And three of the thirty went down and went down to Kadon to David, to the cave of Adullam; and there was a troop of the foreigners, and they encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.23:14: And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the foreigners was then in Bethlehem.
verses.23:15: And David longed and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the cistern that is in Bethlehem, the one at the gate?" Now the company of the foreigners was then in Bethlehem.
verses.23:16: And the three mighty men broke through into the camp of the foreigners and drew water from the cistern that is in Bethlehem, the one at the gate, and took it and came to David, yet he was not willing to drink it; and he poured it out as a drink offering to the Lord.
verses.23:17: And he said, "Far be it from me, Lord, to do this! Should I drink the blood of the men who went at the peril of their lives?" And he was not willing to drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
verses.23:18: And Abishai brother of Joab, son of Zeruiah, he was commander among the three, and he raised up his spear against three hundred wounded men; and he had a name among the three.
verses.23:19: Of those three he was renowned, and he became a commander for them, yet he did not reach the three.
verses.23:20: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada, he was a man of many deeds from Kabzeel, and he struck down the two sons of Ariel of Moab; and he went down and struck the lion in the middle of the pit on the day of snow.
verses.23:21: He struck down the Egyptian man, a conspicuous man; now in the Egyptian's hand was a spear like the beam of a gangplank; and he went down to him with the spear and snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.
verses.23:22: These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
verses.23:23: Of the three he was renowned, yet he did not reach the three; and David appointed him to his hearing. And these are the names of the mighty men of King David:
verses.23:24: Asahel brother of Joab, he was among the thirty; Elhanan son of Dudi his uncle, in Bethlehem;
verses.23:26: Selles the Kelothi; Ira son of Iska, the Tekoite;
verses.23:27: Abiezer the Anothite, from the sons of the Anothite;
verses.23:28: Ellon the Ahohite; Noere the Entophathite.
verses.23:29: Esthai son of Riba from Gibeah, son of Benjamin the Ephrathite;
verses.23:32: Emasu the Salabonite; sons of Asan, Jonathan;
verses.23:33: Samnan the Harodite; Amnan son of Arai, a Saraurite;
verses.23:34: Eliphelet son of the Asbite, son of the Machachaachi; Eliab son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
verses.23:36: Gaal son of Nathan from the army, son of Galaaddi;
verses.23:37: Hadaoi from the brooks; Gadabiel son of the Arabothite. Elie the Ammonite; Gelore the Bethorite, carrying the armor of Joab, son of Zeruiah;
verses.23:38: Ira the Aithirite; Gerab the Etthenite;
verses.23:39: Uriah the Hittite; thirty-seven in all.
verses.24:1: And the Lord caused wrath to be kindled again against Israel, and He incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."
verses.24:2: And the king said to Joab the commander of the force who was with him, "Go through now all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and register the people, and I will know the number of the people."
verses.24:3: And Joab said to the king, "Now may the Lord God add to the people as many as they are and as many as they are a hundredfold, while the eyes of my lord the king are looking on; yet why does my lord the king desire this matter?"
verses.24:4: And the word of the king prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army; and Joab and the commanders of the force went out from before the king to register the people of Israel.
verses.24:5: And they crossed the Jordan and encamped at Aroel, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad and Eliezer.
verses.24:6: And they came to Gilead and to Thabason, which is Nadasai, and they arrived at Dan-idan and Udan, and went around to Sidon.
verses.24:7: And they came to Mapsar of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivite and the Canaanite; and they came toward the south of Judah to Beersheba.
verses.24:8: And they traveled throughout all the land; and they arrived at Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
verses.24:9: And Joab gave the number of the registration of the people to the king; and Israel was eight hundred thousand men of valor drawing the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand fighting men.
verses.24:10: And David's heart struck him after he had counted the people; and David said to the Lord, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done; now, Lord, please remove the lawlessness of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
verses.24:11: And David arose in the morning; and the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,
verses.24:12: "Go and speak to David, saying, 'Thus says the Lord: Three things I am lifting upon you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.'"
verses.24:13: And Gad went in to David, and reported to him and said to him, "Choose for yourself what is to happen: whether three years of famine shall come to you in your land, or for three months you flee before your enemies while they are pursuing you, or there be three days of death in your land. Now therefore know and see what word I should answer to Him who sent me."
verses.24:14: And David said to Gad, "I am greatly hemmed in on every side; I will now fall into the hand of the Lord, for His compassions are exceedingly many, but into the hands of man I will by no means fall."
verses.24:15: And David chose death for himself; and they were the days of the wheat harvest, and the Lord sent death in Israel from early morning until the hour of the midday meal; and the plague began among the people, and there died of the people, from Dan even to Beersheba, seventy thousand men.
verses.24:16: And the angel of God stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, and the Lord relented concerning the calamity and said to the angel who was bringing destruction among the people, "It is enough now; hold back your hand." And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
verses.24:17: And David spoke to the Lord, when he saw the angel striking among the people, and he said, "Look, it is I who have done wrong, and these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand now be against me and against my father's house."
verses.24:18: And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, "Go up and set up an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite."
verses.24:19: And David went up according to the word of Gad, in the manner that the Lord had commanded him.
verses.24:20: And Orna looked out and saw the king and his servants passing along above him; and Orna went out and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.
verses.24:21: And Orna said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" And David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to the Lord." And the plague was restrained from over the people.
verses.24:22: And Orna said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up to the Lord what is good in his eyes; here are the oxen for a burnt offering, and the wheels and the gear of the oxen for wood."
verses.24:23: All these things Orna gave to the king; and Orna said to the king, "May the Lord your God bless you."
verses.24:24: And the king said to Orna, "No, rather I will surely buy it from you for a price, and I will not offer up to my Lord, my God, a burnt offering without cost." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
verses.24:25: And David built an altar there to the Lord, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings; and Solomon added to the altar afterward, because it was small at first. And the Lord heeded the land, and the plague was restrained from over Israel.

notes.1:6: The Greek verb περιέπεσαν is third-person plural ("they happened"); the Hebrew text has the first-person singular ("I happened by chance").
notes.1:9: Greek reads "a terrible darkness has seized me" (σκότος δεινόν), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "anguish" or "cramp."
notes.1:12: Greek reads "over the people of Judah" (τὸν λαὸν Ἰούδα), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "over the people of the Lord."
notes.1:18: Greek omits the title "the Bow" found in the Hebrew text and translates "Book of Jashar" literally as "the Book of the Upright" (βιβλίου τοῦ εὐθοῦς).
notes.1:19: Greek opens David's lament with the imperative "Set up a monument" (Στήλωσον) rather than "The glory/beauty" of the Hebrew text; similarly, v. 21 has "was abhorred" (προσωχθίσθη) and v. 25 has plural "wounded ones" (τραυματίαι).
notes.2:2: Greek identifies her as "Ahinoam the Israelite" (ἡ Ἰσραηλεῖτις), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Jezreelite."
notes.2:5: The Greek text (with Codex Vaticanus) reads "the mercy of God" (τὸ ἔλεος τοῦ θεοῦ) rather than "this kindness/mercy" found in the Hebrew text and other Greek witnesses.
notes.2:9: Greek reads the distinct proper name "Thaseiri" (Θασειρεί) and "Israel" (Ἰσραήλ), corresponding to "the Ashurites" and "Jezreel" in the Hebrew text (see also the doublet "from the camp to Mahanaim" in v. 8).
notes.2:16: Greek translates the Hebrew place name Helkath-hazzurim as "Portion of the Plotters" (Μερὶς τῶν ἐπιβούλων).
notes.2:24: Greek preserves the distinctive names "Amman" (Ἀμμάν) and "Gai" (Γαί) for Hebrew "Ammah" and "Giah"; similarly, v. 29 translates the Hebrew place names Arabah, Bithron, and Mahanaim as "the west," "the entire stretch," and "the camp."
notes.2:31: In this Greek text, "And Asahel" (καὶ Ἀσαήλ) opens v. 31 rather than concluding the tally of David's missing men at the end of v. 30, and the verse ends with "from him" (παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ) instead of "died" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.3:3: The Greek reads Daluia (MT: Chileab), just as 3:2 reads 'the Israelite' (MT: 'the Jezreelitess') and 3:4 reads Orneil son of Pheggith (MT: Adonijah son of Haggith).
notes.3:7: Throughout chapters 3-4 the Greek calls Saul's son Mephibosheth (MT: Ish-bosheth), the same name as Jonathan's son in 4:4; the Greek also preserves distinct names Ial (MT: Aiah), Thailam in 3:12 (MT: 'where he was' or 'on the spot'), Selles in 3:15 (MT: Laish), and Baraki in 3:16 (MT: Bahurim).
notes.3:30: The Greek reads 'were keeping close watch on' (diepareterounto), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'killed'; similarly, in 3:14 and 3:18 'foreigners' (allophyloi) is the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines.
notes.3:34: In 3:33-34 the Greek renders Hebrew nabal ('fool') as the proper name Nabal, reading 'he did not draw near like Nabal' (MT: 'were not put [into fetters]; as one falls'), and reads 'gathered together' where MT has 'wept again'.
notes.3:39: The Greek reads 'a relative and appointed by a king' (syngenes kai kathestamenos hypo basileos), differing notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'weak, though anointed king'.
notes.4:4: The Greek reads 'from Israel' (MT: 'from Jezreel') and uses the masculine noun ho tithenos ('his nurse' or male caretaker) along with the masculine pronoun 'he'.
notes.4:6: The Greek preserves a narrative detail about the female doorkeeper cleaning wheat and falling asleep so Rechab and Baanah slipped past unnoticed, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text states that they entered as though fetching wheat and struck him in the belly.
notes.4:7: The Greek reads 'the road toward the west' (interpreting the Hebrew consonant string for 'the Arabah' as 'evening/west'), and in 4:10 reads 'before me' (MT: 'in his own eyes') and 'a reward for good news' (euangelia).
notes.5:8: The Greek reads "with a dagger" (en paraxiphidi) and explicitly adds "of the Lord" to "the house" (cf. also 5:6, where the blind and the lame "stood in opposition"), diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "water shaft" and shorter saying.
notes.5:13: The Greek text reads "after he came to Hebron" (eis Chebron), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from Hebron."
notes.5:16: Alongside the distinct Septuagint spellings Epidae (MT: Eliada) and Eliphaath (MT: Eliphelet), the Greek appends a thirteen-name duplicate list (Samae through the second Eliphaath) reflecting a parallel tradition related to 1 Chronicles 3:5-8 and 14:4-7.
notes.5:17: Greek allophyloi ("foreigners") is the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines in Judges and Kingdoms; in 5:18 and 5:22, "Valley of the Titans" preserves the distinct Septuagint proper name (MT: Valley of Rephaim).
notes.5:20: The Greek translates the place name as "Upper Breaches" and reads "from the Upper Breaches" (MT: "to Baal-perazim"). Similarly, in 5:23-24 the Greek reads "place/grove of weeping" and "the closing in" (MT: "balsam trees" and "marching"), and in 5:25 "Gibeon" (MT: "Geba").
notes.6:1: The Greek reads "about seventy thousand" young men, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "thirty thousand."
notes.6:2: The Greek renders the Hebrew place name Baale-judah as "from the rulers of Judah in an ascent" and translates the divine title as "Lord of powers" (Kyrios ton dynameon, also in 6:18; MT: "Lord of hosts"). In 6:3, the Greek reads "to the house of Amminadab" (MT: "from the house of Abinadab"; cf. 1 Sam 7:1) and translates the Hebrew name Ahio as "his brothers" (also in 6:4).
notes.6:6: The Greek gives the distinct proper name Nodab (MT: Nachon) and reads "because the calf pulled him aside, in order to hold it" (repeating "to hold it"), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "because the oxen stumbled."
notes.6:10: The Greek gives the distinct proper name Abeddara (vv. 10-12) for the Hebrew Masoretic Text's Obed-edom, and explicitly calls the ark "the ark of the covenant of the Lord."
notes.6:13: The Greek describes "seven choirs" carrying the ark with a sacrifice of a calf and a lamb (and in 6:14 "an unusual robe" rather than "a linen ephod"), differing substantially from the Masoretic Text's "six steps." In 6:22, the Greek reads "in your eyes" (MT: "in my own eyes") and a condensed indirect-speech clause echoing Michal's taunt in 6:20.
notes.7:1: The Greek reads kateklēronomēsen ('gave him an inheritance'), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew verb than the Masoretic Text's 'gave him rest.'
notes.7:11: The Greek uniquely reads oikon oikodomēseis autō ('you will build a house for Him'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'the Lord will make a house for you' (contrast v. 27 below).
notes.7:15: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the Greek omits the name of Saul and reads 'from those whom I removed from before Me,' and in v. 16 continues in the third person ('his house... his kingdom... before Me... his throne') rather than second-person 'your.'
notes.7:18: The Greek reads ēgapēkas me ('You have loved me'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'You have brought me'; similarly in v. 19 the Greek reads 'I was diminished a little' rather than 'this was a small thing.'
notes.7:23: The Greek reads 'another nation' (ethnos allo) and 'nations and dwellings' (ethnē kai skēnōmata), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'one nation' and 'nations and their gods.'
notes.7:26: The Greek text of v. 26 is considerably shorter than the Hebrew Masoretic Text, placing 'Lord Almighty, God of Israel' as a direct address in v. 25 and omitting the clause about David's house being established before God.
notes.8:1: Greek allophyloi literally means 'foreigners' (people of another tribe) and is the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines in 1-2 Kingdoms; 'the set-apart territory' (tēn aphōrismenēn) corresponds to Hebrew Metheg-ammah.
notes.8:2: The Greek reads 'the two measured lines' for both those put to death and those kept alive, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'two lines' to death and 'one full line' kept alive.
notes.8:4: The Greek reads 'one thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen' (matching 1 Chronicles 18:4), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text of 2 Samuel 8:4 reads 'one thousand seven hundred horsemen.'
notes.8:7: Greek chlidōnas means 'bracelets' (unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'shields'), and the closing clause about Shishak taking them is a Septuagint addition that names Jeroboam son of Solomon (Greek Ieroboam, rather than Rehoboam).
notes.8:8: Masbak (Greek Masbak) is a Septuagint-distinct place name followed by 'from the choice cities' (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'Betah and Berothai, cities'), and the second sentence about Solomon's bronze furnishings is a Septuagint addition matching 1 Chronicles 18:8.
notes.8:10: Jedduran (Greek Ieddouran) is a Septuagint-distinct name closer to 'Hadoram' in 1 Chronicles 18:10 (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text of 2 Samuel 8:10 reads 'Joram'), and keimenos ('opposed') likely reflects or abbreviates antikeimenos ('adversary').
notes.8:13: Gebelem (Greek Gebelem) is a Septuagint-distinct place name transliterating the Hebrew phrase for 'Valley of Salt'; in vv. 12-14 the Greek uses Idumea (Idoumaia, the Septuagint name for Edom), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Aram' (Syria) in vv. 12-13.
notes.8:16: Ahijah (Greek Acheia) is a Septuagint-distinct name where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Ahilud.'
notes.8:17: Asa (Greek Asa) is a Septuagint-distinct name where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Seraiah.'
notes.8:18: Janak (Greek Ianak) is a Septuagint-distinct name where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Jehoiada'; the Greek also adds symboulos ('counselor') and renders the office of David's sons as aularchai ('court rulers,' vs. Masoretic 'priests').
notes.9:4: The Greek here spells the father's name Amaer (Amaēr), whereas v. 5 has Ammiel (Ameiēl).
notes.9:11: The Greek reads third-person narration 'at David's table' (with 'one of the king's own sons'), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads first-person 'at my table.'
notes.10:3: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text concludes the spies' supposed aim with "to overthrow it," the Greek reads "to examine it" (kataskepsasthai), providing a third verb of reconnaissance.
notes.10:4: The Greek states simply that Hanun shaved "their beards," without the Masoretic Text's "half of."
notes.10:6: The Greek reads that "the people of David had been put to shame" (MT: that the Ammonites had become odious to David) and names the mercenaries as "Syria and Rehob," "the king of Amalek" (MT: Maacah), and "Istob" (rendering Hebrew "men of Tob" as a single proper name).
notes.10:8: The Greek attaches "of Syria of Zobah" in the genitive directly to "the gate," rather than listing Aram-zobah alongside the allies in the field as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.10:16: The Greek uniquely names the river "Chalamak" (likely a doublet of Helam) before stating that the Syrians came to Helam; similarly in 10:19 the Greek uses a military verb for "defected" (automoleo) rather than "made peace."
notes.11:3: The Greek names Bathsheba's father "Eliab" rather than the Masoretic Text's "Eliam" (and spells Bathsheba as Bersabee).
notes.11:4: The Greek reads "he went in to her" (masculine subject, feminine object), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "she came to him."
notes.11:11: Instead of the Masoretic Text's double oath "as you live and as your soul lives," the Greek opens with the exclamation "How?" (pos) followed by "as your soul lives."
notes.11:21: The Greek reads "Jeroboam son of Ner" (MT: Jerubbesheth) and "Thamasi" (MT: Thebez), and describes the weapon as "a piece of a millstone" (MT: an upper millstone).
notes.11:22: Unlike the Masoretic Text, the Greek narrates the fulfillment of Joab's prediction, reporting David's anger at Joab and his full rebuke to the messenger (here naming Abimelech's father simply "Jeroboam," without "son of Ner").
notes.12:6: Greek reads "sevenfold" (kept also in 4QSam^a), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "fourfold."
notes.12:9: Greek begins with "Because" (linking causally into 12:10) rather than the Masoretic interrogative "Why?" and in 12:10 omits "Me" after "showed contempt."
notes.12:25: Greek renders the name as "Idedei" (Idedei, without the divine suffix), corresponding to Hebrew "Jedidiah."
notes.12:30: Greek preserves both the proper name "Melchol" and "their king," where the Masoretic Text has a single word vocalized either "their king" or "Milcom."
notes.13:15: Greek includes the clause "the last evil greater than the first" (absent from the Masoretic Text), anticipating Tamar's protest in 13:16, where Greek introduces her speech with "concerning this great evil."
notes.13:21: Greek adds "yet he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, because he was his firstborn," a reading supported by 4QSam^a but absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.13:27: Greek adds "And Absalom made a banquet like the banquet of the king," a plus attested in 4QSam^a but absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.13:34: Greek includes the watchman's report naming "the road of Oronen" (probably Horonaim or Beth-horon), a plus supported by 4QSam^a and missing from the Masoretic Text.
notes.13:37: Greek spells the king's name "Tholmailem" (corresponding to Hebrew "Talmai") and adds the place name "to Machad" (absent from the Masoretic Text).
notes.13:39: Greek reads "ceased" (kopazo), giving a clear sense where the Masoretic Hebrew verb is famously debated between "ceased" and "longed."
notes.14:11: The Greek omits any negation before "is multiplied" (plethynthenai), reading literally that the kinsman of blood is multiplied to destroy, whereas the Hebrew MT implies restraining the avenger of blood from multiplying destruction.
notes.14:14: Unlike the Hebrew MT, which negates both clauses ("God does not take away life" and "that a banished one not remain banished"), the Greek omits both negations and states that God will take a life and is devising to banish a banished one from Himself.
notes.14:15: The Greek reads "the people will see me" (reflecting a root meaning "see" rather than MT "fear") and "your people will say" (where the MT has "your maidservant said").
notes.14:17: The Greek reads "for sacrifices" (eis thysias), reflecting a reading of Hebrew minhah ("offering") rather than MT menuhah ("rest/comfort").
notes.14:27: The closing clause ("and she became wife to Rehoboam son of Solomon and bore to him Abiathar") is a Septuagint addition absent from the Hebrew MT and names Rehoboam's son Abiathar rather than Abijam or Abijah (compare 1 Kings 15:1; 2 Chronicles 11:20).
notes.15:12: The Greek identifies Ahithophel as "the Tekonite" (Thekonei) from "Gola" (corresponding to MT "the Gilonite" from "Giloh") and uses "shattering" (syntrimma) where the MT has "conspiracy."
notes.15:18: The Greek preserves an expanded doublet naming "the Chettites" (Chettei, alongside "the Cherethites" later in the verse) and adding the halt "at the olive tree in the wilderness," and it reads "to Gath" (MT "from Gath").
notes.15:19: The Greek spells this Gittite commander's name "Seththi" (Seththei) here and in v. 22 (apparently from dittography of the final sigma of the preceding Greek preposition pros) while using the standard "Ittai" (Eththei) in v. 21.
notes.15:24: The Greek adds the place name "from Baithar" (apo Baithar), likely arising from a textual doublet of the name Abiathar; in the preceding verse (15:23) the Greek renders Kidron first as "of the cedars" (ton kedron) and then as "Kidron" (Kedron).
notes.15:28: The Greek reads "campaigning" (strateuomai, likely an inner-Greek corruption of stranggeuomai, "lingering/waiting") and leaves the Hebrew geographical term araboth ("plains/steppes") untranslated as "Araboth."
notes.15:32: The Greek transliterates Hebrew harosh ("the summit") as a proper name, "Roos" (Rhoos); in v. 34 it also preserves a longer speech ("Your brothers have passed on... let me live") absent from the Hebrew MT.
notes.16:1: Greek transliterates Hebrew rosh ("summit") as the place name Roos and renders the dried fruit as "dates" rather than "summer fruit."
notes.16:11: Greek renders Hebrew "the Benjaminite" (ben-hayemini) literally as "the son of the Jeminite."
notes.16:23: Greek reads "in the former days" rather than "in those days."
notes.17:3: Greek preserves the fuller simile "just as a bride returns to her husband; only you are seeking the life of one man," which differs substantially from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:8: Greek adds the second comparison "and like a fierce sow in the plain," not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:16: "Araboth" transliterates a Hebrew term for plains or fords; "persuade" renders Greek katapeise (Codex Vaticanus), where other Greek witnesses read katapie ("swallow up").
notes.17:19: "Araphoth" transliterates an obscure Hebrew food term, likely crushed grain or groats, which the Greek says the woman "dried" on the covering.
notes.17:25: Greek reads masculine "brother" (adelphou), making Nahash the brother of Zeruiah, whereas the Hebrew reads feminine "sister" referring to Abigail.
notes.17:27: The Greek name "Ouesbei" (Hebrew "Shobi") incorporates the preceding Hebrew conjunction "and" into the name.
notes.17:29: "Sapphoth" transliterates an obscure Hebrew term, likely curds or cheeses of cattle; the Greek also reads singular "he said" rather than plural "they said."
notes.18:14: The Greek preserves a doublet in Joab's opening remark ("This I will begin; I will not wait like this before you") and uses a plural verb ("they thrust") following singular "Joab took," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a singular verb ("he thrust").
notes.18:18: The Greek contains an expanded doublet ("in which he was taken and erected it to take") absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reports Absalom's reason in indirect speech, and renders the monument's name literally as "Hand of Absalom."
notes.18:21: "Cushi" transliterates the Greek proper name Chousei, rendering the Hebrew gentilic "the Cushite" as a personal name; at the end of the verse the Greek also reads "went out" where the Hebrew has "ran."
notes.18:23: "Kechar" transliterates the Greek place name Kechar, which renders Hebrew ha-kikkar ("the plain" or "the Jordan valley") as a proper name.
notes.18:28: The Greek literally reads "who hate their hand" (tous misountas), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew verb as "hated" rather than the Masoretic Text's "lifted up."
notes.19:1: The Septuagint begins chapter 19 here (corresponding to 18:33 in most English Bibles) and renders the Hebrew wish idiom literally as "Who would grant my death in place of you?" (Greek tis doe).
notes.19:10: The Greek text includes "David" and "and from his kingdom" (absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and regularly renders "Philistines" with allophyloi ("foreigners").
notes.19:19: The Greek includes the opening clause "and they performed the service of bringing the king across" (not in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and reads exegeirai ("to rouse") where the Masoretic Text has "to bring across."
notes.19:36: The Greek phrase "to evil" (eis poneron) is a Septuagint doublet alongside "and bad" (kai kakou), both rendering the same Hebrew expression.
notes.19:44: Greek literally reads "ten hands" (an idiom for shares or parts) and contains the notable Septuagint additions "and I am firstborn rather than you" and "ahead of Judah," which are absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.20:6: Greek reads "overshadow our eyes" (skiasei tous ophthalmous hemon), reflecting a Hebrew root meaning "to shade" rather than the Masoretic Text's "escape from our sight."
notes.20:14: The Greek reads the place name "Charri" (en Charrei) and a singular verb "he came," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "the Berites" (or Bichrites) and has a plural verb.
notes.20:18: The Septuagint preserves a much longer form of the proverb than the Hebrew Masoretic Text, explicitly mentioning "and in Dan" and "whether the things that the faithful of Israel established had failed."
notes.20:23: The Greek text names Benaiah's father as "Ahilud" (Acheilouth, matching verse 24), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jehoiada."
notes.20:25: The Greek text names the scribe as "Joshua" (Greek Iesous), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Sheva" (Kethib "Sheya").
notes.21:1: The Greek syntax is elliptical ("injustice on account of him, by a death of bloodshed"), differing from the Hebrew reading of bloodguilt on Saul and his house.
notes.21:6: The Greek reads "Gibeon of Saul" (rather than Hebrew "Gibeah of Saul") and plural "chosen ones of the Lord" referring to the seven men; "expose in the sun" renders the specific Greek verb exeliazō (also in vv. 9, 13-14).
notes.21:8: The Greek has the distinct name "Serei" where the Hebrew reads "Adriel."
notes.21:11: The closing clause ("and they grew faint, and Dan the son of Joa...") is a Septuagint addition absent from the Hebrew text, introducing the distinct names Dan and Joa.
notes.21:12: The Greek reads "Beth" (lacking the second element of Hebrew "Beth-shan"), and renders Hebrew "Philistines" with allophyloi ("foreigners") here and in vv. 15 and 17-19, its standard term in 1-2 Kingdoms.
notes.21:14: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name "Zela" as a common noun, "in the side."
notes.21:18: The Greek reads "Gath" (Hebrew "Gob") and the distinct proper name "Oebocha the Hastatothite" (Hebrew "Sibbecai the Hushathite").
notes.21:19: The Greek reads the distinct proper names "Rom" (Hebrew "Gob"), "Ariorgim" (Hebrew "Jaare-oregim"), and "Godolias the Hittite" (Hebrew "Goliath the Gittite").
notes.21:20: The Greek treats the Hebrew expression for "a man of stature" as a proper name, "a man of Madon."
notes.22:2: The Greek text includes the introductory rubric Ode ("A song") between "And he said" and the vocative "Lord," reflecting a Septuagint canticle heading not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.22:30: Where the Hebrew reads "troop" or "raiding band," the Greek has the nominative adjective monozonos ("lightly armed," literally "single-girded"), describing an agile light-armed soldier.
notes.22:32: Where the Hebrew reads "rock," the Greek translates with ktistes ("creator") and adds the future verb "will be" (compare phylax, "guardian," in vv. 3 and 47).
notes.22:36: The Greek reads "Your listening" (hypakoe) rather than "Your gentleness," and includes the verbless phrase "into a broad place for my steps beneath me" at the end of v. 36 rather than at the start of v. 37.
notes.22:51: This Greek text concludes 22:51 with the introductory clause "And these are the last words of David," which is usually placed at the opening of 23:1.
notes.23:1: In this Greek text the introductory clause 'And these are the last words of David' appears at the end of 22:51 rather than opening 23:1; the Septuagint also reads 'Faithful' (pistos) instead of 'oracle', reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants, and renders 'over the anointed' rather than 'raised on high'.
notes.23:3: The Greek diverges markedly from the Masoretic Text here and in 23:4, rendering 'Rock of Israel' as 'Guardian from Israel', reading 'Speak a parable' for 'one who rules', and reading 'fear of the anointed' (christou) rather than 'fear of God'.
notes.23:9: The Greek reads Elhanan (MT: Eleazar) and uses 'the foreigners' (hoi allophyloi), the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines in 1-2 Kingdoms. At the end of the verse, 'cried out' (aneboesen) differs from MT 'withdrew'.
notes.23:21: The Greek uniquely describes the Egyptian's spear as 'like the beam of a gangplank' (xylon diabathras) and states that Benaiah went down to him 'with the spear' rather than 'with a club'.
notes.23:25: Throughout 23:8-38 the Greek preserves numerous distinctive personal and place names (such as Jebosthe, Adinon, Theria, Kadon, Saima the Rudite, Selles, Noere, Esthai, Emasu, and Gelore), omits 23:30 (with surviving elements appearing in 23:29 and 23:37), and in 23:36 translates 'from Zobah' as 'from the army' (apo dynameos).
notes.24:5: In 24:5-7 the Greek preserves distinctive place names compared to the Masoretic Text: Aroel (MT: Aroer), Eliezer (MT: toward Jazer), Thabason which is Nadasai (MT: land of Tahtim-hodshi), Dan-idan and Udan (MT: Dan-jaan and around), and transliterated Mapsar of Tyre (MT: fortress of Tyre).
notes.24:13: The Septuagint reads 'three years of famine' (matching 1 Chronicles 21:12) rather than 'seven years' as in the Masoretic Text, and renders 'pestilence' literally as 'death' (thanatos) here and in 24:15.
notes.24:15: The Greek includes clauses absent from the Masoretic Text ('And David chose death for himself; and they were the days of the wheat harvest... and the plague began among the people') and reads 'until the hour of the midday meal' (horas aristou) instead of 'until the appointed time'.
notes.24:16: The Greek consistently names the Jebusite 'Orna' (MT: Araunah; 1 Chronicles: Ornan) throughout 24:16-24. In 24:21 the final clause is an indicative statement ('And the plague was restrained') rather than a purpose clause inside David's speech.
notes.24:25: The sentence 'and Solomon added to the altar afterward, because it was small at first' is a Septuagint addition not found in the Masoretic Text.
